magisterium.assessment_en: The description of evangelization and work with preschool-age children does not in itself contradict Catholic teaching; the Church recognizes that even young children can be open to God and that the faith is transmitted through example, prayer, and appropriate instruction. Nevertheless, the passage describes the project, but does not state its content or method of implementation, so it cannot be assessed to what extent Eho Kids truly transmits the integral Catholic faith.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic youth formation should be rooted in an encounter with Christ, include prayer, community, and service, and remain faithful to Church teaching; these guidelines can also be applied to the assessment of a children's program, although the passage provides no details for such an assessment. Church teaching also emphasizes that a young child can be open to the mystery of God and that the family has the primary educational and evangelizing responsibility, so work with children should support, not replace, that role of parents.
concerns_en: There is no information about who runs the program, how the content is aligned with the teaching of the Church, nor how the instruction is adapted to children aged three to six; these are unknowns, not established problems.

sections.subtitle_en: From preschoolers to university students: a realized dream called Eho Kids
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko speaks with enthusiasm about the Eho Kids project for children aged three to six
sections.content_en:
In addition to educational programs, the association organizes **spiritual retreats, evangelization, and youth work**: with high schoolers, university students, older people, and children. Marko emphasizes that the range is “wide”.

A special pride of his is the **Eho Kids** project, intended for preschoolers aged three to six. Krunoslav remarks that it is “a very interesting crew”. Marko admits that this project “lay closest to his heart” and that he was overjoyed when they launched it last year, because it had been his dream for the last four to five years. He hopes that the project will continue.

Despite numerous projects, the goal remains the same: *“formation of believers and that enthusiasm for Christ and practically holding to that”*.

sections.subtitle: Eho konferencija, Probudi i konferencija za žene
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Krunoslav spominje Eho konferenciju, a Marko najavljuje sljedeće izdanje u Mozaik Event Centru
sections.content:
Krunoslav ističe **Eho konferenciju** koja se održava gotovo svake godine. Marko ga ispravlja: održava se **svake godine**. Sljedeća će biti 13. prosinca u **Mozaik Event Centru**, a riječ je, kako kaže, vjerojatno o četrnaestom izdanju. Prva je održana 2014., prije jedanaest godina, dok je ekipa još bila dio **Zajednice Dobri pastir**.

Tada nastalo ime ostalo je i nakon osamostaljenja. Marko objašnjava da je Eho dio njegove osobne vizije i identiteta koji je zadržao. Ideja je da *„sve što radimo odjekne“*.

Eho konferencija je glavni događaj u godini, ali nije jedini:

- **Probudi**, konferencija za srednjoškolce i studente, koju Marko opisuje kao „najhajpaniju“, „napucanu“ i „snažnu“ za tu generaciju;
- **konferencija za žene**;
- povremena dodatna događanja tijekom godine, „što se već sjetimo i ubacimo“.

Krunoslav zaključuje da je to iznimno mnogo projekata za udrugu koju još uvijek smatra mladom.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak pretežno iznosi podatke o konferenciji i značenju njezina naziva te ne sadrži tvrdnje koje bi bile u sukobu s katoličkim naukom ili Svetim pismom. Spominjanje evangelizacije mladih općenito je u skladu s poslanjem Crkve, premda ovaj ulomak ne objašnjava izričito njezin sadržaj ni usmjerenost na Krista.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko shvaćanje evangelizacije uključuje svjedočenje za Krista riječima i životom, kao i djela milosrđa; kršćansko poslanje nije samo osobna vizija ili organizacijski uspjeh. Zato naziv i identitet konferencije mogu biti korisni ako služe zajedništvu Crkve i navještaju Evanđelja, čiji plodovi pripadaju cijeloj Crkvi.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage predominantly presents information about the conference and the meaning of its name and contains no claims that would conflict with Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. Mentioning the evangelization of young people is generally in accordance with the mission of the Church, although this excerpt does not explicitly explain its content or Christ-centeredness.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of evangelization includes witnessing to Christ through words and life, as well as works of mercy; Christian mission is not merely a personal vision or organizational success. Therefore, the name and identity of the conference can be useful if they serve the communion of the Church and the proclamation of the Gospel, whose fruits belong to the entire Church.

sections.subtitle_en: Eho Conference, Probudi and Conference for Women
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Krunoslav mentions the Eho Conference, and Marko announces the next edition at Mozaik Event Centar
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav highlights the **Eho Conference**, which is held almost every year. Marko corrects him: it is held **every year**. The next one will be on December 13 at the **Mozaik Event Centar**, and it is, as he says, probably the fourteenth edition. The first was held in 2014, eleven years ago, while the team was still part of **Zajednica Dobri pastir**.

The name created back then remained even after gaining independence. Marko explains that Eho is part of his personal vision and identity that he retained. The idea is that *„everything we do echoes“*.

The Eho Conference is the main event of the year, but it is not the only one:

- **Probudi**, a conference for high school and university students, which Marko describes as the „most hyped“, „packed“, and „powerful“ for that generation;
- **conference for women**;
- occasional additional events during the year, „whatever we think of and throw in“.

Krunoslav concludes that this is an exceptionally large number of projects for an association he still considers young.

sections.subtitle: Kad je lider dobro, svi dobivaju
sections.screenshot_description: Marko citira rečenicu s GLS-a o tome da od dobrog stanja lidera koristi imaju svi
sections.content:
Krunoslav prelazi na temu koja se provlači kroz projekte udruge: **liderstvo muškarca**. Podsjeća da su se često susretali na GLS-ovima i da Marko o tome redovito govori na konferencijama. Pita ga zašto je danas važno da se muškarac pokrene kao lider.

Marko odgovara rečenicom koju je čuo na GLS-u: *„Kad je lider dobro, svi dobivaju.“* Ne zna je li riječ o sloganu ili nečijem citatu, ali to vidi u vlastitom okruženju: *„Kad sam ja dobro, mislim da je svima dobro.“*

Kao potvrdu navodi riječi supruge **Mirjane** s nedavnog putovanja s prijateljima u Italiju. Dok su se vozili, rekla mu je: *„Stvarno se isplati moliti za tvoje blagoslove, jer Marko, kad tebi dobro ide, onda svi imamo koristi od toga okolo.“*

Zato smatra da lider mora stalno ulagati u sebe, učiti se i razvijati te ne smije ostati na istoj razini. Od toga koristi imaju tim, ljudi koje vodi, kojima služi i s kojima surađuje. Isto vrijedi za muškarce općenito. Po Markovu mišljenju najgore je kad netko kaže: *„Ja sam takav i to je to, nemam ja prostora za napredak.“* Za muškarca kao glavu obitelji i autoritet to je posebno važno.

Krunoslav tu ubacuje ogradu da je riječ o **duhovnom autoritetu**, „da se ne bi napalili ljevičari“. Marko se nadovezuje šalom da već ima „traume od izvlačenja rečenica na javnim televizijama“. Potvrđuje da misli na duhovni autoritet, odnosno na lidera u vlastitoj obitelji.

magisterium.assessment: Ideja da dobrobit vođe utječe na ljude oko njega može biti razumna, ali sama rečenica ne objašnjava što znači biti „dobro” niti potvrđuje da će svima biti dobro zato što je vođa dobro. Izraz je stoga uglavnom spojiv s katoličkim naukom, uz potrebu da se muško vodstvo shvati kao služenje, a ne kao samodostatnost ili povlastica.
concerns: Tvrdnja „Kad sam ja dobro, mislim da je svima dobro” može zvučati kao da je dobrobit obitelji ili zajednice određena stanjem muškarca-lidera; bez dodatnog konteksta nije jasno radi li se o osobnom opažanju ili općem načelu.
Odlomak ne navodi da autoritet uključuje odgovornost za dobro drugih, poniznost i spremnost na služenje, pa se njegova teološka usklađenost može procijeniti samo djelomično.
magisterium.enrichment: U kršćanskom shvaćanju vodstvo se ne mjeri time koliko se drugi oslanjaju na vođu, nego time kako vođa služi njihovu dobru: crkveni dokument o poslovnom vodstvu uspoređuje takvo služenje s Isusovim pranjem nogu učenicima. Papa Franjo također ističe da se kršćaninova vlast i služenje trebaju sjediniti te da je zajedničko dobro važan kriterij odluka vođe. Zato osobna zrelost muškarca može koristiti njegovoj obitelji, ali nije zamjena za uzajamno poštovanje i brigu za svakog člana.

citations.document_title: Vocation of the Business Leader: A Reflection
citations.document_author: Dicastery for Promoting Integral Human Development

citations.document_title: To a Delegation of French Catholic entrepreneurs

magisterium.assessment_en: The idea that a leader's well-being affects the people around him can be reasonable, but the sentence itself does not explain what it means to be „well” nor does it confirm that everyone will be well because the leader is well. The expression is therefore largely compatible with Catholic teaching, with the need for male leadership to be understood as service, rather than as self-sufficiency or privilege.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In the Christian understanding, leadership is not measured by how much others rely on the leader, but by how the leader serves their good: a Church document on business leadership compares such service to Jesus washing the feet of the disciples. Pope Francis also emphasizes that a Christian's authority and service should be united and that the common good is an important criterion for a leader's decisions. Therefore, a man's personal maturity can benefit his family, but it is not a substitute for mutual respect and care for each member.
concerns_en: The claim „When I am well, I think everyone is well” can sound as though the well-being of the family or community is determined by the condition of the male leader; without additional context, it is not clear whether it is a personal observation or a general principle.
The passage does not state that authority includes responsibility for the good of others, humility, and a readiness to serve, so its theological alignment can only be partially assessed.

sections.subtitle_en: When the Leader Is Well, Everyone Wins
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko quotes a sentence from the GLS about how everyone benefits from the leader being in a good state
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav moves on to the topic that runs through the association's projects: **a man's leadership**. He reminds that they often met at the GLSes and that Marko regularly speaks about this at conferences. He asks him why today it is important for a man to get moving as a leader.

Marko responds with a sentence he heard at the GLS: *„When the leader is well, everyone wins.“* He does not know whether it is a slogan or someone's quote, but he sees it in his own environment: *„When I am well, I think everyone is well.“*

As confirmation, he cites the words of his wife **Mirjana** from a recent trip with friends to Italy. While they were driving, she told him: *„It really pays off to pray for your blessings, because Marko, when you are doing well, then all of us around you benefit from it.“*

That is why he considers that a leader must constantly invest in himself, learn and develop, and must not remain at the same level. From that, the team, the people he leads, whom he serves, and with whom he collaborates benefit. The same applies to men in general. In Marko's opinion, the worst thing is when someone says: *„I am like that and that's it, I have no room for progress.“* For a man as the head of the family and authority, this is especially important.

Krunoslav here inserts a caveat that it is about **spiritual authority**, „so that the leftists don't get worked up“. Marko follows up with a joke that he already has „traumas from sentences being pulled out on public television“. He confirms that he means spiritual authority, that is, a leader in his own family.

sections.subtitle: Lekcija od sina Jošue: djeca upijaju ono što jesmo
sections.screenshot_description: Marko opisuje trenutak kad je sin Jošua ponovio njegovu lošu naviku
sections.content:
Stalni rad na sebi Marko opravdava jednostavnom logikom: *„Sve što mi jesmo, ćemo prenositi dalje.“* Pitanje je samo što želimo prenijeti. Kaže da na njegov razvoj najviše utječu njegovi sinovi.

Opisuje situaciju koja ga je, kako kaže, „baš prepala“. Sin **Jošua** ponovio je nešto za njim, a radilo se o navici koju Marko nikako nije želio prenijeti. Tada je shvatio da sin upija ono što u njemu vidi. Zaključio je da se mora zapitati što želi da dijete upije i da mora mijenjati sebe i vlastite obrasce ponašanja kako bi sin preuzeo dobar obrazac.

*„Oni će upiti ono što ja jesam. I meni je to dovoljna motivacija da ne prestajem raditi na sebi, da otkrivam sebe, svoje obrasce i da ih mijenjam i da, kako ono kažu popularno, budem najbolja verzija sebe.“*

Krunoslav to sažima ovako: djeca, kao i drugi ljudi, ne preuzimaju ono što im govorimo da bi trebali biti, nego ono što zapravo jesmo. Slijede naš primjer i oponašaju nas.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom: naglašava da roditeljski primjer oblikuje djecu i da je osobni rad na sebi dio odgovornog roditeljstva. Tvrdnju da djeca upijaju ono što vide valja razumjeti kao snažan utjecaj, a ne kao neizbježan ili potpun prijenos roditeljskih navika.
concerns: Izjava „Sve što mi jesmo, ćemo prenositi dalje“ može zvučati preopćenito ako se shvati kao da djeca automatski usvajaju roditeljske obrasce; kršćansko razumijevanje odgoja uključuje i djetetovu osobnu slobodu.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva uči da roditelji imaju prvu odgovornost za odgoj djece te da njihov dobar primjer, uz spremnost priznati vlastite pogreške, posebno pomaže u tom poslanju. Biblijska i crkvena perspektiva ne svodi odgoj na oponašanje: roditelji svjedoče vjeru i oblikuju djecu, ali se ona postupno i slobodno osobno odazivaju Božjem pozivu.

citations.document_title: 9 July 2006: Holy Mass in Valencia on the occasion of the Fifth World Meeting of Families

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic teaching: it emphasizes that parental example shapes children and that personal work on oneself is part of responsible parenting. The claim that children absorb what they see should be understood as a strong influence, and not as an inevitable or complete transmission of parental habits.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church teaches that parents have the primary responsibility for the upbringing of children and that their good example, along with a readiness to admit their own mistakes, particularly assists in this mission. The biblical and ecclesial perspective does not reduce upbringing to imitation: parents witness to the faith and form children, but they gradually and freely respond personally to God's call.
concerns_en: The statement „Everything that we are, we will pass on“ may sound too generalized if understood as meaning that children automatically adopt parental patterns; the Christian understanding of upbringing also includes the child's personal freedom.

sections.subtitle_en: A lesson from son Jošua: children absorb what we are
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko describes the moment when his son Jošua repeated his bad habit
sections.content_en:
Marko justifies constant work on oneself with simple logic: *„Everything that we are, we will pass on.“* The only question is what we want to pass on. He says that his sons have the greatest influence on his development.

He describes a situation that, as he says, „really scared“ him. His son **Jošua** repeated something after him, and it was about a habit that Marko by no means wanted to pass on. Then he realized that his son absorbs what he sees in him. He concluded that he must ask himself what he wants the child to absorb and that he must change himself and his own behavior patterns so that his son would adopt a good pattern.

*„They will absorb what I am. And to me that is sufficient motivation not to stop working on myself, to discover myself, my patterns and to change them and to, as they popularly say, be the best version of myself.“*

Krunoslav summarizes it like this: children, like other people, do not adopt what we tell them they should be, but what we actually are. They follow our example and imitate us.

sections.subtitle: Zašto muškarci više ne zovu djevojke na kavu
sections.screenshot_description: Marko govori o strahu od odbacivanja kao temeljnom strahu muškarca
sections.content:
Krunoslav postavlja aktualno pitanje: zašto su muškarci sve suzdržaniji, sve rjeđe zovu djevojke na kavu i nedostaje im liderske komponente u tom dijelu života? Zašto se boje pristupiti djevojci?

Marko korijen problema vidi u **strahu od odbijanja i odbacivanja**, koji je, kaže, temeljan „pogotovo kod nas muškaraca“. Neuspjeh u pokušaju za muškarca je *„dosta duboko poniženje“*. Ljudi na to reagiraju različito. Neki ostanu uporni i ne odustaju, a drugi se zatvore i upadnu u pasivnost: *„Pokušao sam, nije uspjelo i neću ništa napraviti po tom pitanju.“* Prema njegovu mišljenju, isti obrazac vrijedi i u mnogim drugim područjima života.

Drugi problem je **izbjegavanje odgovornosti**. Marko naglašava da to nije samo muški problem, nego problem društva, i da je kod nas posebno izražen, i u obitelji i u ovakvim situacijama. Odgovornost znači nositi se s posljedicama, znati ih iskanalizirati i riješiti te pogledati sebe. To se potom pretvara u borbu s identitetom i s onim kako se osjećamo nakon neuspjeha. Spominje i predavanje koje je nedavno slušao, u kojem je govornik upravo strah od odbacivanja naveo kao razlog zbog kojeg se muškarci ne upuštaju u nova osvajanja i pothvate.

Krunoslav dodaje da muškarci nakon odbijanja često odu u jedan od dva ekstrema: ili se potpuno zatvore ili pokušavaju osvojiti svaku djevojku pošto-poto. Zlatne sredine, primjećuje, nema.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom spojiv s katoličkim pogledom jer prepoznaje strah i obeshrabrenje kao stvarna ljudska iskustva, a ne kao nešto što samo po sebi znači manjak vjere ili moralni prijestup; ipak, opis straha kao osobito muškog i neuspjeha kao dubokog poniženja ostaje psihološko tumačenje, a ne katolički nauk.
concerns: Tvrdnja da je strah od odbijanja osobito temeljan kod muškaraca može zvučati kao opća tvrdnja o muškoj naravi, ali ovaj odlomak ne daje osnovu za takvo teološko ili univerzalno zaključivanje.
Riječ poniženje može pretjerano povezati odbijanje s gubitkom dostojanstva; dostojanstvo osobe ne ovisi o tome prihvati li druga osoba poziv.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje ne poriče strah, nego poziva na njegovo razlučivanje i na to da strah ne postane razlog za zatvaranje i trajnu pasivnost; vjera može pomoći osobi da se suoči sa životnim izazovima, iako ne jamči da će poziv biti prihvaćen. U odnosima je važno pristupati drugoj osobi s poštovanjem i bez pritiska, a vlastitu vrijednost ne mjeriti uspjehom udvaranja; kršćanska ljubav ne traži vlastiti interes i čuva dostojanstvo drugoga.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely compatible with the Catholic view because it recognizes fear and discouragement as real human experiences, and not as something that in itself signifies a lack of faith or a moral offense; nevertheless, the description of fear as especially male and failure as deep humiliation remains a psychological interpretation, rather than Catholic teaching.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic understanding does not deny fear, but calls for its discernment and that fear does not become a reason for closing off and permanent passivity; faith can help a person face life's challenges, although it does not guarantee that an invitation will be accepted. In relationships, it is important to approach the other person with respect and without pressure, and not to measure one's own worth by the success of courtship; Christian love does not seek its own interest and preserves the dignity of the other.
concerns_en: The claim that the fear of rejection is particularly foundational in men may sound like a general assertion about male nature, but this passage does not provide a basis for such a theological or universal conclusion.
The word humiliation may excessively link rejection to a loss of dignity; the dignity of a person does not depend on whether the other person accepts an invitation.

sections.subtitle_en: Why men no longer ask girls out for coffee
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko speaks about the fear of rejection as a foundational fear of a man
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks a timely question: why are men increasingly restrained, asking girls out for coffee less and less often, and lacking a leadership component in that part of life? Why are they afraid to approach a girl?

Marko sees the root of the problem in the **fear of refusal and rejection**, which, he says, is foundational "especially among us men." Failure in an attempt is for a man *"a rather deep humiliation."* People react to this differently. Some remain persistent and do not give up, while others close off and fall into passivity: *"I tried, it didn't work, and I won't do anything about it."* In his opinion, the same pattern applies in many other areas of life as well.

The second problem is **avoidance of responsibility**. Marko emphasizes that this is not only a men's problem, but a problem of society, and that it is especially pronounced among us, both in the family and in situations like this. Responsibility means dealing with the consequences, knowing how to channel and resolve them, and looking at oneself. This then turns into a struggle with identity and with how we feel after failure. He also mentions a lecture he recently listened to, in which the speaker cited fear of rejection precisely as the reason why men do not engage in new conquests and endeavors.

Krunoslav adds that after rejection, men often go to one of two extremes: either they completely close off or they try to win over every girl at all costs. There is, he notes, no golden mean.

sections.subtitle: Pet godina upornosti: kako je Marko osvojio Mirjanu
sections.screenshot_description: Marko otkriva da je dan snimanja upravo osma godišnjica njegova braka
sections.content:
Krunoslav zamoli gosta da podijeli „mini svjedočanstvo“ o tome kako je godinama osvajao suprugu **Mirjanu**. Marko u šali kaže da ga odbijanja „nisu baš potresla“. Ozbiljnije objašnjava da je uporan i u drugim područjima: prepreka za njega nije kraj priče, nego povod da smisli kako doći do cilja, makar sve trenutno govorilo da ne može. Osvajanje je trajalo oko **pet godina**.

Tijekom razgovora otkriva da je dan snimanja upravo **osma godišnjica braka**. Krunoslav se našali da je baš taj dan odlučio doći na podcast, a Marko dodaje da ga je supruga taman pitala kad misli doći doma.

Ograđuje se da to nije savjet za sve. Netko s trideset godina neće sljedećih pet ili šest godina čekati da se druga osoba odluči. Marko je tada imao 19 godina i nije mu se žurilo. Upravo je izašao iz duge veze, pa je bio, kako kaže, „na prisilnom samovanju“, što danas smatra dobrim za sebe.

Mirjana mu je stalno govorila da ima skrivene namjere. On joj je odgovarao da ništa ne skriva jer joj je rekao sve: sve što radi, radi jer je osvaja. Ona se ipak nije mogla opustiti ni razviti povjerenje. Marko je pokušavao svakih nekoliko mjeseci, *„A sad? A sad? A sad?“*, sve dok **nakon četiri godine** nije potpuno odustao. Tek tada je u njoj „nešto proradilo“.

Mirjana je imala **dva sna** u kojima joj je, kako Marko prenosi, Bog jasno pokazao da je on taj za kojeg se treba odlučiti. Istodobno joj je poručeno da mu ništa ne smije reći i da ga mora pustiti na miru dok se sam ne predomisli. Marko je u to vrijeme ušao u vezu, kako kaže, „uletio“ u nju jer je htio krenuti dalje, ali u njoj nije vidio budućnost i prekinuo ju je. Mirjana mu ni tada ništa nije govorila. Nakon nekoliko mjeseci Marko je odlučio pokušati još jednom i tada je, **2015. godine**, krenulo.

I to je imalo zaplet. Mirjana je rekla „da, može“, a zatim „a nisam sigurna“. Marko smatra da mu je Bog dao milost da u tom trenutku dobro reagira: *„Ma nema veze, uzmi si vremena, pričekat ćemo.“* Od tada su zajedno, deset godina, od čega osam u braku.

magisterium.assessment: Opis je uglavnom spojiv s katoličkim naukom: ustrajnost i nada same po sebi nisu problem, a odlomak ne kaže da je Marko prisiljavao Mirjanu ili zanemarivao njezinu slobodu. Ipak, budući da se spominju višegodišnje odbijanje i „osvajanje“, važno je da se upornost ne shvati kao pravo nastaviti pritiskati osobu koja je jasno odbila odnos, jer brak zahtijeva slobodan pristanak.
concerns: Izraz „osvajao suprugu“ i isticanje da ga odbijanja nisu potresla mogu se, bez dodatnog konteksta, protumačiti kao romantiziranje ustrajnog udvaranja unatoč odbijanju; odlomak ne daje dovoljno pojedinosti da bi se zaključilo je li Mirjanina sloboda bila poštovana.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje braka podrazumijeva slobodan pristanak obiju osoba; Rimska rota izričito naglašava da se ženidbeni savez ne može sklopiti bez slobodnog čina volje. Kristov primjer također povezuje poziv s poštovanjem slobode: privlačio je učenike strpljivo, a ne prisilom. Zato se ustrajnost može vrednovati kao strpljenje i iskrenost samo dok istodobno poštuje granice i slobodan odgovor druge osobe.

citations.document_title: Decisiones seu Sententiae, Tomus LXXXVIII (Annus Decisionum: 1996)

magisterium.assessment_en: The description is generally compatible with Catholic teaching: perseverance and hope in themselves are not a problem, and the passage does not say that Marko coerced Mirjana or disregarded her freedom. However, since multi-year rejection and "winning over" are mentioned, it is important that persistence is not understood as a right to continue pressuring a person who has clearly rejected a relationship, because marriage requires free consent.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of marriage entails the free consent of both persons; the Roman Rota explicitly emphasizes that the marital covenant cannot be entered into without a free act of the will. Christ's example also links calling with respect for freedom: He attracted the disciples patiently, not by coercion. Therefore, perseverance can be valued as patience and sincerity only as long as it simultaneously respects boundaries and the other person's free response.
concerns_en: The phrase "won his wife over" and the emphasis that the rejections did not shake him can, without additional context, be interpreted as a romanticization of persistent courtship despite rejection; the passage does not provide enough details to conclude whether Mirjana's freedom was respected.

sections.subtitle_en: Five years of persistence: how Marko won Mirjana over
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko reveals that the recording day is precisely the eighth anniversary of his marriage
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks the guest to share a "mini-testimony" about how he won his wife **Mirjana** over through the years. Marko jokingly says that the rejections "didn't really shake" him. More seriously, he explains that he is persistent in other areas as well: an obstacle for him is not the end of the story, but an occasion to figure out how to reach the goal, even if everything currently says he cannot. The pursuit lasted about **five years**.

During the conversation, he reveals that the recording day is precisely their **eighth wedding anniversary**. Krunoslav jokes that he decided to come to the podcast on that very day, and Marko adds that his wife had just asked him when he planned to come home.

He qualifies this by saying that this is not advice for everyone. Someone who is thirty years old will not wait for the next five or six years for the other person to make up their mind. Marko was 19 years old at the time and was in no rush. He had just come out of a long relationship, so he was, as he says, "in forced singlehood," which he considers good for himself today.

Mirjana kept telling him that he had hidden intentions. He would reply to her that he was hiding nothing because he told her everything: everything he does, he does because he is courting her. She, however, could not relax nor develop trust. Marko tried every few months, *“What about now? What about now? What about now?”*, until **after four years** he completely gave up. Only then did "something kick in" inside her.

Mirjana had **two dreams** in which, as Marko conveys, God clearly showed her that he was the one she should decide on. At the same time, she was told that she must not tell him anything and that she had to leave him alone until he changed his mind on his own. Marko entered a relationship at that time, as he says, "jumped" into it because he wanted to move on, but he saw no future in it and broke it off. Mirjana still did not say anything to him even then. After a few months, Marko decided to try once more, and that was when, in **2015**, things took off.

Even that had a twist. Mirjana said "yes, okay," and then "well, I'm not sure." Marko believes that God gave him the grace to react well at that moment: *“Never mind, take your time, we'll wait.”* Since then they have been together, ten years, of which eight in marriage.

sections.subtitle: Mirjanin strah od nesigurnog života ovisnog o donacijama
sections.screenshot_description: Marko objašnjava čega se Mirjana bojala kad je ulazila u vezu s njim
sections.content:
Krunoslav primjećuje da su nakon početka veze brzo uslijedile zaruke i vjenčanje. Marko potvrđuje da su oboje bili svjesni da veza vodi prema braku. Upravo toga se Mirjana bojala.

Marko je već tada pokazivao u kojem će smjeru ići njegov život i da će biti posvećen onome čemu je i danas posvećen. Mirjana je, kaže, htjela *„sve samo ne takvu nesigurnost“*. Željela je miran i siguran život, a Markov put značio je ovisnost o **donacijama i podršci**, uz osjećaj da „sve visi nad glavom“.

Nesigurnost je imala i svoj godišnji ritam. Dvije do tri godine zaredom, u isto doba godine, pred rujan, trajala bi dva do tri mjeseca strepnje: *„Ide dalje, ne ide dalje, šta ću onda, kako će biti?“* Krunoslav dobacuje da mu je ta priča jako poznata.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak prvenstveno opisuje Mirjanin strah od financijske nesigurnosti i sam po sebi ne tvrdi ništa protiv katoličkog nauka: strah i želja za stabilnošću nisu automatski znak manjka vjere. Budući da je tekst nepotpun, nije moguće procijeniti kako se u nastavku vrednuju poziv, donacije ili odgovornost prema budućoj obitelji.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje poziva uključuje i brak i druge oblike služenja; nijedan se ne smije prikazivati kao obveza da se zanemari odgovorno razlučivanje ili obiteljske dužnosti. Crkveni nauk o velikodušnosti istodobno upozorava da davanje ne treba biti takvo da osobu optereti preko mjere, pa povjerenje u Boga nije isto što i nepromišljeno prihvaćanje financijskog rizika.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage primarily describes Mirjana's fear of financial insecurity and in itself asserts nothing against Catholic teaching: fear and the desire for stability are not automatically a sign of a lack of faith. Since the text is incomplete, it is not possible to assess how vocation, donations, or responsibility toward a future family are evaluated further on.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of vocation includes both marriage and other forms of service; neither should be portrayed as an obligation to neglect responsible discernment or family duties. At the same time, the Church's teaching on generosity warns that giving should not be such that it burdens a person beyond measure, so trust in God is not the same as the reckless acceptance of financial risk.

sections.subtitle_en: Mirjana's fear of an insecure life dependent on donations
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko explains what Mirjana was afraid of when entering into a relationship with him
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav notes that after the relationship began, engagement and marriage quickly followed. Marko confirms that both of them were aware that the relationship was leading toward marriage. That was precisely what Mirjana feared.

Marko was already showing back then which direction his life would take and that he would be dedicated to what he is dedicated to today. Mirjana, he says, wanted *„anything but such insecurity“*. She wanted a peaceful and secure life, and Marko's path meant dependence on **donations and support**, along with the feeling that "everything hangs over one's head".

Insecurity also had its annual rhythm. Two to three years in a row, at the same time of year, before September, there would be two to three months of anxiety: *„Does it go on, does it not go on, what will I do then, how will it be?“* Krunoslav interjects that this story is very familiar to him.

sections.subtitle: Korona, depresija i supruga koja je vjerovala
sections.screenshot_description: Marko se prisjeća krize za vrijeme korone i Mirjanine podrške
sections.content:
Kad je jednom prihvatila takav život, Mirjana mu je postala velika podrška. Marko to najbolje vidi na primjeru razdoblja **korone**, o kojem su razgovarali i na dan snimanja.

Tada je, priznaje, bio **u depresiji**, a da toga nije ni bio svjestan. Sve se zaustavilo. Udruga se bavi edukacijama i nastupima pred ljudima, a odjednom ništa nije funkcioniralo. Otvarala su se pitanja hoće li donatori nastaviti davati i hoće li se udruga morati ugasiti. Istodobno je stao i Mirjanin posao, edukacija javnog nastupa, koja se također odvija uživo.

Mirjana mu je tada rekla nešto čega su se nedavno ponovno prisjetili: *„Ja sam vjerovala da ćeš ti to izvući na kraju i da će biti dobro.“* Tako je i bilo. Od **2020. do 2022.** sve je krenulo uzlazno i stabiliziralo se. Marko kaže da ni danas ništa nije posve sigurno, ali je stanje „onako sigurno“.

Zaključuje s dozom ironije da je Mirjana predosjetila da bi tako moglo biti i htjela je to izbjeći, ali je na kraju ipak „završila u tome“ s njim. Krunoslav dodaje: *„Predosjete žene mnogo toga.“*

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak iznosi osobno iskustvo depresije, poslovne neizvjesnosti i bračne podrške, bez tvrdnji koje bi bile u suprotnosti s katoličkim naukom ili Svetim pismom. Prikaz suprugine potpore u teškoći u skladu je s kršćanskim shvaćanjem bračne solidarnosti, premda odlomak sam po sebi ne iznosi izričito teološko tumačenje tih događaja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje depresije može priznati njezinu duhovnu težinu, ali je ne svodi na duhovni problem niti je smatra znakom manjka vjere; oboljelima valja pristupati strpljivo i pružati odgovarajuću podršku. Crkva također prepoznaje da financijske i radne teškoće mogu opteretiti obiteljski život te da supružnicima u krizama mogu pomoći milost, pomirenje i podrška drugih.

citations.document_author: Catholic Bishops’ Conference of England and Wales

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage presents a personal experience of depression, business uncertainty, and marital support, without claims that would be contrary to Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. The portrayal of the wife's support in hardship is in accordance with the Christian understanding of marital solidarity, although the passage itself does not explicitly present a theological interpretation of these events.
magisterium.enrichment_en: A Catholic understanding of depression can acknowledge its spiritual weight, but does not reduce it to a spiritual problem nor consider it a sign of a lack of faith; sufferers should be approached patiently and provided with appropriate support. The Church also recognizes that financial and work difficulties can burden family life and that spouses in crises can be helped by grace, reconciliation, and the support of others.

sections.subtitle_en: Corona, depression and a wife who believed
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko recalls the crisis during corona and Mirjana's support
sections.content_en:
Once she accepted such a life, Mirjana became a great support to him. Marko sees this best in the example of the **corona** period, which they also talked about on the day of filming.

At that time, he admits, he was **in depression**, without even being aware of it. Everything stopped. The association deals with education and performances before people, and suddenly nothing worked. Questions opened up about whether donors would continue to give and whether the association would have to shut down. At the same time, Mirjana's work also stopped, public speaking training, which also takes place live.

Mirjana then said something to him that they recently recalled again: *„I believed that you would pull this off in the end and that it would be fine.“* And so it was. From **2020 to 2022**, everything started an upward path and stabilized. Marko says that even today nothing is completely certain, but the situation is „sort of certain“.

He concludes with a dose of irony that Mirjana sensed that it could be like that and wanted to avoid it, but in the end still „ended up in it“ with him. Krunoslav adds: *„Women sense many things.“*

sections.subtitle: Dva poduzetnika, dvoje djece i život u kontra smjenama
sections.screenshot_description: Marko opisuje razdoblje kad su se supružnici izmjenjivali u brizi za djecu
sections.content:
Krunoslav pita kako danas izgleda njihova svakodnevica kad su oboje lideri, on u udruzi, a ona u vlastitom poslu, uz djecu i, kako kaže, apostolate.

Marko odgovara jednom riječju: **„Teško.“** Zahtjevno je jer su oboje poduzetnici. Kao čelnik udruge ne zna unaprijed odakle će doći novac i ne odrađuje samo svoj posao, nego mora smisliti i financiranje. Isto vrijedi za Mirjanu, koja ima **vlastitu firmu za edukacije**. Po struci je **profesorica hrvatskog jezika i retorike**. Marko ju je potaknuo da ne ide raditi u školu, nego da pokrene vlastiti posao, jer je u tome, kaže, „vrhunska“.

Najteže je bilo nakon rođenja sinova, najprije **Jošue**, a zatim i drugog sina, **Jana**. Postoji razdoblje od osam do devet mjeseci u kojem Mirjana ponovno počinje raditi, Marko radi, a dijete još ne ide u vrtić. Tada su radili u kontra smjenama: *„Nekad bude šest dana, mi smo samo spavali doma u krevetu u isto vrijeme.“* Netko je uvijek morao biti s djecom, a stalnu pomoć u čuvanju nemaju, osim kod većih prilika.

Marko iskreno priznaje da nisu uvijek imali razumijevanja jedno za drugo. U tim intenzivnim razdobljima „pucaju po šavovima“, a to se odražava na odnos jer se ne viđaju, ne komuniciraju i nemaju zajedničkog vremena. Ključ opstanka vidi u **međusobnom razumijevanju, podršci i jasnom dogovoru**: *„Gle, to je sad takvo vrijeme, ti trebaš svoje stiskati, ja imam svoje.“* U takvim razdobljima vide se tek nedjeljom, kad su svi zajedno.

Zbog edukacija, putovanja i duhovnih obnova Marko je jedno vrijeme morao ograničiti izbivanja na **dva puta mjesečno** i doslovno odbijati sve ostale pozive kako bi sačuvao vrijeme s obitelji. *„Zahtjevno je, ali je moguće“*, zaključuje, dok god se razumiju, podržavaju i oboje prihvaćaju takav stil života. Ipak dodaje: *„Izazovno je, borbeno.“*

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak opisuje zahtjevnost poduzetničkog i obiteljskog života, ali ne iznosi tvrdnju koja bi proturječila katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu. Budući da je prikaz djelomičan i ne govori kako supružnici usklađuju posao, apostolat i obiteljske obveze, njegova se cjelovita usklađenost ne može procijeniti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje braka naglašava uzajamnu odgovornost supružnika, zajedničko razlučivanje i skladan odnos koji se razvija kroz svakodnevni život; zato su dogovor i pravedna podjela obveza važni i u zahtjevnim poslovnim okolnostima. Crkva također upozorava da zauzetost poslom ili društvenim djelovanjem ne bi smjela potisnuti vrijeme i skrb koji pripadaju supružniku i djeci.

citations.document_title: The Bible and Morality: Biblical Roots of Christian Conduct
8 April 1987: Holy Mass for families in Córdoba, Argentina - Homily

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage describes the demanding nature of entrepreneurial and family life, but does not state an assertion that would contradict Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture. Since the account is partial and does not state how the spouses harmonize work, apostolate, and family obligations, its complete alignment cannot be assessed.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of marriage emphasizes the mutual responsibility of spouses, shared discernment, and a harmonious relationship that develops through daily life; therefore, agreement and a fair division of obligations are important even in demanding business circumstances. The Church also warns that busyness with work or social activity should not crowd out the time and care that belong to the spouse and children.

sections.subtitle_en: Two entrepreneurs, two children, and life in opposite shifts
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko describes the period when the spouses took turns caring for the children
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks what their everyday life looks like today when both are leaders, he in an association and she in her own business, along with children and, as he says, apostolates.

Marko answers in one word: **„Difficult.“** It is demanding because both are entrepreneurs. As the head of an association, he does not know in advance where the money will come from and does not just do his job, but also has to figure out the financing. The same applies to Mirjana, who has **her own educational training company**. By profession, she is a **professor of the Croatian language and rhetoric**. Marko encouraged her not to go work in a school, but to start her own business, because, he says, she is „top-notch“ at it.

It was most difficult after the birth of their sons, first **Jošua**, and then their second son, **Jan**. There is a period of eight to nine months in which Mirjana starts working again, Marko works, and the child does not yet go to kindergarten. Back then, they worked in opposite shifts: *„Sometimes there are six days, we only slept at home in bed at the same time.“* Someone always had to be with the children, and they do not have permanent babysitting help, except on major occasions.

Marko honestly admits that they did not always have understanding for each other. In those intense periods they „burst at the seams,“ and that is reflected in the relationship because they do not see each other, do not communicate, and have no time together. He sees the key to survival in **mutual understanding, support, and a clear agreement**: *„Look, it's such a time now, you need to push through yours, I have mine.“* In such periods, they only see each other on Sundays, when everyone is together.

Due to trainings, travels, and spiritual retreats, Marko had to limit his absences for a time to **twice a month** and literally decline all other invitations in order to preserve time with his family. *„It is demanding, but it is possible“*, he concludes, as long as they understand each other, support each other, and both accept such a lifestyle. Yet he adds: *„It is challenging, combative.“*

sections.subtitle: Brak otključava razine kao u videoigri
sections.screenshot_description: Marko slikovito objašnjava kako brak i djeca otključavaju skrivene obrasce ponašanja
sections.content:
Krunoslav pita je li ga osobno iskustvo potaknulo da se bavi partnerskim odnosima i gdje se u njima „najviše lome koplja“. Marko kaže da mu je to od početka bila draga tema jer uvijek izaziva reakciju: ljudi se ili slažu ili ne slažu, ali to žele čuti. Ipak priznaje da mu je današnje iskustvo potpuno drugačije nego na početku, jer svaka životna faza budi stvari kojih čovjek prije nije bio svjestan.

Prvi problem vidi u tome što **u Hrvatskoj nemamo dobru pripremu za brak**. Najbliže dubljem razgovoru je, prema njegovu mišljenju, zaručnički vikend Zajednice bračnih susreta. Za neke se stvari može pripremiti unaprijed, ali mnoge se otključaju tek u braku.

Kao banalan, ali slikovit primjer navodi dogovor o krpi za pod. U njegovoj obitelji čistilo se krpom, a u Mirjaninoj džogerom. Dogovorili su se za džoger. Poanta je u tome da dvije osobe iz dviju različitih obitelji odjednom stalno žive zajedno. Svatko donosi svoje navike i vlastitu sliku braka, uglavnom upijenu od roditelja.

Marko taj proces opisuje usporedbom iz videoigara: *„Otključao se kao razina na igrici, odjednom si dobio novo oružje.“* Ulaskom u brak otvaraju se obrasci ponašanja i uvjerenja kojih čovjek nije bio svjestan, a s djecom se otvara još jedan sloj.

Navodi osobni primjer. Postojala je stvar koju nije volio kod svog oca i koja ga je živcirala. U jednoj situaciji s Jošuom napravio je potpuno isto. *„Ne mogu vjerovati da sam napravio isto to. A zašto? Zato što sam to gledao.“* Iako mu se to ponašanje nije sviđalo, upio ga je, a dijete ga je „triggeriralo“.

Zaključuje da svaka faza donosi nove izazove i da je ključno imati znanje i alate kojima se može otkriti što se događa, odakle to dolazi i što treba mijenjati.

magisterium.assessment: Dostupni ulomak uglavnom je neutralan: naglašava da iskustvo odnosa i braka mijenja čovjekovo razumijevanje kroz životne faze, što je spojivo s katoličkim shvaćanjem braka kao odnosa koji se trajno izgrađuje. Procjena je ograničena jer se odlomak prekida usred rečenice, pa se ne može pouzdano utvrditi što autor tvrdi o problemima pripreme za brak niti kako razvija metaforu „otključavanja razina“.
concerns: Metafora braka kao igre koja „otključava razine“ može biti neprimjerena ako brak prikazuje kao osobni napredak ili nagradu, umjesto kao trajni poziv na uzajamno predanje; iz dostupnog ulomka nije jasno da autor doista tako misli.
Prekinuta rečenica („u Hrvatskoj nemamo...“) onemogućuje procjenu glavne kritike ili konkretnog teološkog sadržaja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička priprava za brak obuhvaća duhovnu i moralnu formaciju te praktičnu pripremu za zajednički život, roditeljstvo i teškoće bračnog odnosa; brak se ne može svesti na spontanu odluku ili pojedinačno iskustvo. Crkveni nauk opisuje bračni odnos kao odnos muškarca i žene koji se treba trajno razvijati, uz vjernost, isključivost i plodnost.

citations.document_title: Preparation for the sacrament of marriage
Preparation for the sacrament of marriage

magisterium.assessment_en: The available excerpt is generally neutral: it emphasizes that the experience of relationships and marriage changes a person's understanding through life stages, which is compatible with the Catholic understanding of marriage as a relationship that is continuously built. The assessment is limited because the passage breaks off mid-sentence, so it cannot be reliably determined what the author claims about the problems of marriage preparation nor how he develops the metaphor of "unlocking levels."
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic marriage preparation includes spiritual and moral formation as well as practical preparation for life together, parenting, and the difficulties of the marital relationship; marriage cannot be reduced to a spontaneous decision or individual experience. Church teaching describes the marital relationship as a relationship between a man and a woman that should continually develop, along with fidelity, exclusivity, and fruitfulness.
concerns_en: The metaphor of marriage as a game that "unlocks levels" may be inappropriate if it portrays marriage as personal advancement or a reward, instead of as a lasting call to mutual self-giving; from the available excerpt it is not clear that the author truly means this.
The interrupted sentence ("in Croatia we do not have...") prevents the assessment of the main criticism or specific theological content.

sections.subtitle_en: Marriage unlocks levels like in a video game
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko vividly explains how marriage and children unlock hidden behavioral patterns
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav asks whether personal experience prompted him to deal with partner relationships and where in them "spears are broken the most." Marko says that from the beginning this was a dear topic to him because it always provokes a reaction: people either agree or disagree, but they want to hear it. Still, he admits that his experience today is completely different than at the beginning, because every life phase awakens things a person was not aware of before.

He sees the first problem in the fact that **in Croatia we do not have good marriage preparation**. The closest thing to a deeper conversation, in his opinion, is the betrothal weekend of the Zajednica bračnih susreta. For some things one can prepare in advance, but many are unlocked only in marriage.

As a banal but vivid example, he cites the agreement about a floor cloth. In his family, cleaning was done with a cloth, and in Mirjana's with a mop. They agreed on the mop. The point is that two persons from two different families suddenly live together constantly. Everyone brings their own habits and their own image of marriage, mostly absorbed from parents.

Marko describes this process with a comparison from video games: *"It unlocked like a level in a game, suddenly you got a new weapon."* By entering into marriage, patterns of behavior and beliefs of which a person was not aware open up, and with children yet another layer opens up.

He gives a personal example. There was a thing he did not like about his father and that annoyed him. In one situation with Jošua he did completely the same thing. *"I can't believe I did the exact same thing. And why? Because I watched that."* Although he did not like that behavior, he absorbed it, and the child "triggered" it.

He concludes that every phase brings new challenges and that it is crucial to have the knowledge and tools with which one can discover what is happening, where it comes from, and what needs to be changed.

sections.subtitle: Iza fasade savršene katoličke obitelji
sections.screenshot_description: Marko otvoreno govori o vlastitim problemima i odlasku na psihoterapiju
sections.content:
Marko o braku rado govori jer je, kako ističe, **brak u Hrvatskoj u krizi**. Odlazak u crkvu ne znači nužno dobar brak, a o tome se šuti. Ljudi čuvaju *„sliku idealne katoličke obitelji“* u kojoj su svi sretni, a zapravo ne razgovaraju, udaljeni su, hladni ili „totalno u drugim filmovima“. Boje se priznati probleme pred drugim „savršenim“ katoličkim obiteljima.

Marko sam ide u suprotnom smjeru. U programima otvoreno govori o svojim padovima i greškama. Kad je krenuo na **psihoterapiju**, morao je nagovoriti terapeuta, kojeg osobno poznaje, da ga primi. Na pitanje hoće li mu smetati što će se otkriti neke stvari o njemu odgovorio je: *„80 posto stvari sam izrekao u nekom programu negdje. Ako ti iščupaš ovih 20, molim te, izvuci ih van.“*

Spominje i podcast o seksu nakon kojeg su dobili „more uvreda“, između ostalog i zbog same riječi. Upravo zato smatra važnim o takvim temama govoriti iskreno, kako bi ljudi imali mjesto gdje mogu priznati da i sami imaju problema. Kad je nedavno pred nekoliko prijatelja otvoreno iznio vlastiti problem i slomljenost, bili su šokirani. Jedan mu je rekao: *„Puno sam se toga pronašao, ali nisam mogao to iskomunicirati i reći.“*

*„Mi se možemo praviti super divni, krasni molitveni timovi. Što se to događa iza zatvorenih vrata? To mene zanima“*, kaže Marko. Služba i pomazanje su važni, ali jednako je važna autentičnost privatnog života. Kad privatno nešto ne štima, on se, priznaje, osjeća „kao najveći licemjer“. Poruka je ipak jasna: *„Okej je da nije sve okej.“* I u njihovu su braku bila razdoblja kad su, kako kaže, bili „katastrofa“ i morali se izboriti i isplivati. *„Evo sad se ispovijedam“*, dodaje. Krunoslav se nadovezuje: *„Taman na godišnjicu braka.“*

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem braka jer ne poistovjećuje odlazak u crkvu s automatski skladnim bračnim životom i potiče iskrenost o teškoćama umjesto održavanja privida. Prikaz psihoterapije kao pomoći nije u suprotnosti s vjerom; ipak, budući da se odlomak prekida, nije moguće procijeniti što je govornik dalje rekao.
concerns: Tvrdnja da je brak u Hrvatskoj u krizi široka je činjenična ocjena koju sam odlomak ne potkrepljuje, pa je treba razumjeti kao govornikovu procjenu, a ne kao ovdje dokazanu činjenicu.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveno učenje priznaje da obiteljski život može biti obilježen krizom, usamljenošću i udaljenošću te poziva na suosjećajno praćenje, a ne na osuđivanje ili idealiziranje stvarnosti. Ivan Pavao II. izričito navodi da se u bračnoj krizi može potražiti pomoć posebno osposobljenih psihologa i psihoterapeuta, uz istodobno oslanjanje na milost i ljubav Duha Svetoga.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of marriage because it does not equate going to church with an automatically harmonious married life and encourages honesty about difficulties instead of maintaining appearances. The presentation of psychotherapy as an aid does not contradict faith; however, because the passage cuts off, it is not possible to assess what the speaker said further.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching recognizes that family life can be marked by crisis, loneliness, and distance, and calls for compassionate accompaniment rather than judging or idealizing reality. John Paul II explicitly states that in a marital crisis, the help of specially trained psychologists and psychotherapists may be sought, while at the same time relying on the grace and love of the Holy Spirit.
concerns_en: The claim that marriage in Croatia is in crisis is a broad factual assessment that the passage itself does not substantiate, so it should be understood as the speaker's assessment rather than a fact proven here.

sections.subtitle_en: Behind the facade of the perfect Catholic family
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko speaks openly about his own problems and going to psychotherapy
sections.content_en:
Marko gladly speaks about marriage because, as he points out, **marriage in Croatia is in crisis**. Going to church does not necessarily mean a good marriage, and people remain silent about this. People preserve the *"image of the ideal Catholic family"* in which everyone is happy, while in reality they do not talk, are distant, cold, or "totally in different films". They are afraid to admit problems in front of other "perfect" Catholic families.

Marko himself goes in the opposite direction. In programs, he speaks openly about his falls and mistakes. When he started **psychotherapy**, he had to persuade the therapist, whom he knows personally, to take him in. To the question of whether it would bother him that some things about him would be revealed, he replied: *"80 percent of things I have stated in some program somewhere. If you pluck out these 20, please, pull them out."*

He also mentions a podcast about sex after which they received a "sea of insults", among other things because of the word itself. Precisely because of that, he considers it important to speak honestly about such topics, so that people would have a place where they can admit that they themselves have problems. When he recently openly presented his own problem and brokenness in front of a few friends, they were shocked. One of them told him: *"I found myself in a lot of that, but I couldn't communicate and say it."*

*"We can pretend to be super wonderful, gorgeous prayer teams. What is happening behind closed doors? That is what interests me"*, Marko says. Ministry and anointing are important, but the authenticity of private life is equally important. When something is not right privately, he admits, he feels "like the biggest hypocrite". The message is nevertheless clear: *"It's okay that not everything is okay."* In their marriage, too, there were periods when, as he says, they were a "disaster" and had to fight through and surface. *"Here I am now confessing"*, he adds. Krunoslav chimes in: *"Just in time for the wedding anniversary."*

sections.subtitle: Tajni računi i financijski stres koji snižava inteligenciju
sections.screenshot_description: Marko iznosi rezultate istraživanja o parovima sa zajedničkim i razdvojenim financijama
sections.content:
Prelazeći na financije, Krunoslav pita oko čega se bračni parovi najviše „kolju“. Marko odgovara: **oko tajnosti**, odnosno kad supružnici nisu upoznati s financijama jedno drugoga.

Pozivajući se na istraživanja na koja je naišao pripremajući predavanje za nedavnu konferenciju, navodi da **financijski stres doslovno smanjuje kvocijent inteligencije**, točnije radnu memoriju za razmišljanje. Zbog toga donosimo lošije odluke, a to se prelijeva na odnos kroz povlačenje, šutnju, netrpeljivost i ljutnju. Posebno opterećuje dugoročan dug, kad se ne radi o iznosu koji će se vratiti sljedeći mjesec.

Opisuje i istraživanje na, kako se prisjeća, **230 parova** prosječne dobi oko 28 godina na početku braka:

- trećina je imala **zajedničke financije**;
- trećina je bila **upoznata s financijama** jedno drugoga;
- trećina je imala **razdvojene financije**.

Nakon dvije godine ponovljen je test zadovoljstva. Parovi sa zajedničkim financijama imali su najbolje rezultate, *„daleko puno bolje“* od onih s razdvojenim financijama.

Razdvojene financije, prema Marku, ostavljaju mnogo prostora za skrivanje i „padanje u grijeh“: kocku, nepotrebno trošenje, stvaranje dugova i loše upravljanje novcem. Kad još netko vidi stanje, postoji određena kontrola. Ne radi se o nadgledniku, nego o tome da *„barem još netko vidi“*.

Posebno upozorava na **kockanje**. Poznaje nekoliko bliskih slučajeva muškaraca koji su upali u ogromne dugove i uništili obitelji. *„To nisu ljudi koji su tamo daleki ovisnici. To su ljudi u crkvi svaki dan.“* Prokockali su, kaže, more novca, automobile i stanove.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom sukladan katoličkom razumijevanju braka jer naglašava otvorenost među supružnicima i prepoznaje kako materijalne teškoće mogu opteretiti obiteljske odnose. Tvrdnja da financijski stres „doslovno smanjuje kvocijent inteligencije” nije teološki problem sama po sebi, ali u prikazanom odlomku nije potkrijepljena izvorom i zahtijeva znanstveno preciznije formuliranje.
concerns: Izraz „doslovno smanjuje kvocijent inteligencije” može pretjerano pojednostaviti tvrdnju o učinku stresa na radnu memoriju; dostavljeni izvori ne potvrđuju tu znanstvenu tvrdnju.
Odlomak je prekinut usred rečenice, pa procjena obuhvaća samo dostupni dio.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko shvaćanje braka kao zajednice čitavog života daje osnovu za isticanje iskrenog i odgovornog razgovora o financijama, iako odlomak ne razrađuje konkretne moralne obveze supružnika u upravljanju novcem. Crkveni nauk također prepoznaje da oskudica i materijalne teškoće mogu ugroziti obiteljski život te naglašava potrebu da se supružnicima kod kojih su nastale takve teškoće pruži olakšanje; stoga financijski stres treba shvatiti ozbiljno, ali ne i svoditi bračne sukobe isključivo na novac.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is generally aligned with the Catholic understanding of marriage because it emphasizes openness between spouses and recognizes how material difficulties can burden family relationships. The claim that financial stress "literally reduces intelligence quotient" is not a theological problem in itself, but in the presented passage it is not substantiated by a source and requires a scientifically more precise formulation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of marriage as a partnership of the whole of life provides a basis for highlighting honest and responsible conversation about finances, although the passage does not elaborate on the specific moral obligations of spouses in money management. Church teaching also recognizes that deprivation and material difficulties can jeopardize family life and emphasizes the need to provide relief to spouses in whom such difficulties have arisen; therefore, financial stress should be taken seriously, but marital conflicts should not be reduced exclusively to money.
concerns_en: The phrase "literally reduces intelligence quotient" may oversimplify the claim about the effect of stress on working memory; the provided sources do not confirm this scientific claim.
The passage is cut off in the middle of a sentence, so the assessment covers only the available part.

sections.subtitle_en: Secret accounts and financial stress that lowers intelligence
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko presents research results on couples with joint and separate finances
sections.content_en:
Moving on to finances, Krunoslav asks what married couples "fight" over the most. Marko answers: **over secrecy**, that is, when spouses are not familiar with each other's finances.

Referring to research he came across while preparing a lecture for a recent conference, he states that **financial stress literally reduces intelligence quotient**, more precisely the working memory for thinking. Because of this, we make worse decisions, and this spills over into the relationship through withdrawal, silence, intolerance, and anger. Long-term debt is particularly burdensome, when it is not an amount that will be paid back next month.

He also describes research on, as he recalls, **230 couples** with an average age of about 28 at the beginning of marriage:

- a third had **joint finances**;
- a third were **familiar with finances** of each other;
- a third had **separate finances**.

After two years, the satisfaction test was repeated. Couples with joint finances had the best results, *"far, much better"* than those with separate finances.

Separate finances, according to Marko, leave a lot of room for hiding and "falling into sin": gambling, unnecessary spending, accumulating debt, and poor money management. When someone else also sees the situation, there is a certain control. It is not about an overseer, but about the fact that *"at least someone else sees"*.

He particularly warns about **gambling**. He knows several close cases of men who fell into huge debts and destroyed families. *"Those are not people who are distant addicts over there. Those are people in church every day."* They gambled away, he says, a sea of money, cars, and apartments.

sections.subtitle: Granica od 20 eura i glas razuma za nove tenisice
sections.screenshot_description: Marko objašnjava kako on i Mirjana dogovaraju trošenje novca
sections.content:
Marko otkriva kako to funkcionira kod njih. Nemaju zajednički račun, ali imaju dogovoreni iznos, otprilike **do 20 eura**, za koji ne moraju pitati drugoga. Sve iznad toga moraju reći. Ne radi se o traženju odobrenja, nego o informiranju: *„E, znaš šta, treba mi to, kupit ću nešto.“*

Za neke kupnje treba mu i savjet, priznaje uz smijeh: *„Ja bih rado potrošio na još jedne tenisice i treba mi neki glas razuma koji će mi reći: E, Marko, mislim da je to pretjerivanje.“* Isto vrijedi i u obrnutom smjeru.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim pogledom na brak jer prikazuje dogovor, međusobno informiranje i traženje savjeta kao dio zajedničkog života supružnika. Sam opis odvojenih računa i dogovorenog iznosa za osobne kupnje ne pokazuje teološki problem, premda kratki isječak ne govori dovoljno da bi se procijenilo kako supružnici donose šire financijske odluke.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko razumijevanje braka podrazumijeva trajnu uzajamnu odgovornost: supružnici trebaju uzimati u obzir potrebe i sklonosti jedno drugoga, rješavati razlike te odgovorno odlučivati o obiteljskom životu. Dogovor o obavještavanju i savjetovanju može biti konkretan način življenja te odgovornosti, a ne puko traženje dopuštenja. Važno je da pravila o novcu služe uzajamnom poštovanju i zajedničkom dobru, a ne tajnovitosti ili jednostranom nadzoru.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with the Catholic view of marriage because it depicts agreement, mutual informing, and seeking advice as part of the spouses' shared life. The description itself of separate accounts and an agreed-upon amount for personal purchases does not present a theological problem, although the short excerpt does not say enough to evaluate how the spouses make broader financial decisions.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic understanding of marriage implies lasting mutual responsibility: spouses should take into account each other's needs and inclinations, resolve differences, and responsibly make decisions about family life. An agreement on notifying and consulting can be a concrete way of living that responsibility, and not merely asking for permission. It is important that rules about money serve mutual respect and the common good, rather than secrecy or one-sided control.

sections.subtitle_en: The 20-euro limit and the voice of reason for new sneakers
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko explains how he and Mirjana agree on spending money
sections.content_en:
Marko reveals how it works with them. They do not have a joint account, but they have an agreed-upon amount, approximately **up to 20 euros**, for which they do not have to ask the other. Everything above that they have to mention. It is not about asking for approval, but about informing: *„Hey, you know what, I need this, I'm going to buy something.“*

For some purchases he also needs advice, he admits with laughter: *„I would gladly spend on another pair of sneakers and I need some voice of reason to tell me: Hey, Marko, I think that's an exaggeration.“* The same applies in reverse.

sections.subtitle: Kartice i rate nasuprot gotovini: kako je Mirjana promijenila Markov pogled na novac
sections.screenshot_description: Marko uspoređuje financijske navike svoje i Mirjanine obitelji
sections.content:
Marko priznaje da mu se pogled na financije uz Mirjanu **drastično promijenio**. Došao je iz obitelji u kojoj su se koristile kartice, krediti i rate. Mirjana dolazi iz obitelji u kojoj vrijedi pravilo: *ako nemamo dovoljno novca odmah, ne kupujemo*. Karticu na rate ima, ali, kako kaže Marko, ni ne zna gdje joj je. Kod nje je samo „cash and carry“.

Morali su naći sredinu. Kad su podizali kredit, Marko joj je morao objasniti: *„Mirjana, nećemo ga otplatiti za pet godina.“* Kredit se ne može riješiti preko noći. Može se štedjeti, odvajati sa strane i zatvarati dio po dio, ali Mirjanin strah od takvog opterećenja bio je velik i trebalo ga je dovesti „u neku normalu“.

Zahvaljujući njezinim navikama Marko je, kaže, svoj odnos prema novcu bitno popravio. Danas misli da je stvar „više-manje u kontroli“. Upravlja novcem mudrije, bez odlaska u krajnosti, s jasnom idejom gdje ulagati, što davati i kako trošiti. Supružnici su danas, zaključuje, „na istoj valnoj duljini“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim načelima jer prikazuje supružnike kako uvažavaju različite navike i traže zajedničko rješenje u obiteljskim financijama. Samo korištenje kartica, kupnja na rate ili podizanje kredita nije samo po sebi ni moralno pogrešno ni dokaz financijske mudrosti; procjena ovisi o okolnostima i odgovornosti kojom se dug preuzima.
concerns: Odlomak je prekinut prije dovršetka objašnjenja o otplati kredita, pa nije moguće procijeniti njegovu svrhu, uvjete ni jesu li supružnici mogli realno podmirivati obveze.
magisterium.enrichment: Biblijska mudrost upozorava da se posuđeni novac treba vratiti i da neodgovorno zaduživanje može povrijediti povjerenje, ali ne proglašava svaki zajam nedopuštenim (Sir 29,2–6). U braku je važno odluke o novcu donositi uz uzajamnu odgovornost, poštovanje i rješavanje razlika, a ne samo nametati navike jedne obitelji drugoj.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely aligned with Catholic principles because it depicts spouses respecting different habits and seeking a common solution in family finances. The mere use of cards, purchasing in installments, or taking out a loan is in itself neither morally wrong nor proof of financial wisdom; the evaluation depends on the circumstances and the responsibility with which debt is assumed.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Biblical wisdom warns that borrowed money must be repaid and that irresponsible borrowing can harm trust, but it does not declare every loan illicit (Sir 29:2–6). In marriage, it is important to make decisions about money with mutual responsibility, respect, and resolving differences, rather than simply imposing the habits of one family upon the other.
concerns_en: The passage is cut off before the explanation regarding the loan repayment is completed, so it is not possible to evaluate its purpose, terms, or whether the spouses could realistically meet their obligations.

sections.subtitle_en: Cards and installments versus cash: how Mirjana changed Marko's view of money
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko compares the financial habits of his and Mirjana's families
sections.content_en:
Marko admits that his view of finances **drastically changed** with Mirjana. He came from a family where cards, loans, and installments were used. Mirjana comes from a family where the rule applies: *if we do not have enough money right away, we do not buy*. She has an installment card, but, as Marko says, she does not even know where it is. With her it is only "cash and carry".

They had to find a middle ground. When they were taking out a loan, Marko had to explain to her: *"Mirjana, we will not pay it off in five years."* A loan cannot be resolved overnight. One can save, set aside, and pay off part by part, but Mirjana's fear of such a burden was great and it had to be brought "into some sort of normalcy".

Thanks to her habits Marko has, he says, significantly improved his attitude toward money. Today he thinks that the matter is "more or less under control". He manages money more wisely, without going to extremes, with a clear idea of where to invest, what to give, and how to spend. The spouses are today, he concludes, "on the same wavelength".

sections.subtitle: Neka novcem upravlja sposobniji i nije sramota tražiti pomoć
sections.screenshot_description: Marko poručuje da novcem treba upravljati sposobniji partner, bez obzira na to je li to muž
sections.content:
Ovdje Marko ponavlja misao iz uvodnog isječka. Kad jedan partner ne zna upravljati novcem, neka to prepusti onome tko zna. Uobičajeno je mišljenje da je muškarac lider i glava, ali *„ima muškaraca koji ne znaju upravljati novcima, a ako je žena sposobnija, daj njoj da ona upravlja novcima“*. Ako muž uporno troši i srlja, rješenje nije da žena pasivno kaže *„on je glava, neka on odluči“*, nego da preuzme upravljanje. *„Inače ćete biti u problemima.“*

Na nedavnom predavanju o financijama poručio je: ako vam stalno curi, ako ste stalno u minusu i u dugovima i „vrtite iz šupljeg u prazno“, **potražite pomoć**. *„Nije to sramota.“* Savjetuje razgovor s nekim tko će pogledati stanje sa strane i reći što treba srezati i dovesti u red. Sramota je, kaže, bojati se tražiti pomoć, a ne priznati da ne znamo.

Kao primjer navodi poznanika koji upravlja bogatstvom **nogometaša** i drugih bogatih ljudi koji ne znaju što bi s novcem. Imati novac ne znači biti „najpametniji na svijetu“. Isto vrijedi na manjim razinama: može se pitati stručnjaka ili prijatelja koji dobro upravlja novcem. Iz dugova se ne izlazi preko noći, jer se u njima nismo ni našli preko noći, pa treba plan i taktika.

Navodi i otrežnjujući primjer **braka koji se raspao** dok su supružnici bili u dvadesetima, nakon samo nekoliko godina. Jedna osoba nije znala ništa o financijama i dobivala je samo džeparac, a na kraju su se pojavili veliki dugovi i kaos. *„Opasno je područje“*, zaključuje Marko, i savjetuje parovima da razgovaraju i uče o novcu, *„jer se o tome uči“*.

magisterium.assessment: Poruka je uglavnom usklađena s katoličkim pogledom na brak jer praktičnu odgovornost za obiteljske financije veže uz sposobnost, a ne uz spol, te upozorava na štetu neodgovornog trošenja. Ipak, izraz da žena „preuzme upravljanje” treba razumjeti u sklopu zajedničkog razgovora i odgovornog odlučivanja supružnika, a ne kao opravdanje za jednostranu kontrolu ili isključivanje drugoga.
concerns: Odlomak ne pojašnjava treba li promjena u upravljanju novcem biti dogovorena; bez takva pojašnjenja izraz „neka ona upravlja” mogao bi se shvatiti kao jednostrano odlučivanje.

Spominjanje muškarca kao „glave” nije samo po sebi dovoljno razrađeno da bi se procijenilo kako govornik razumije tu biblijsku sliku; ona ne bi smjela opravdavati zanemarivanje uzajamnog poštovanja i odgovornosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički naglasak nije na tome da financijama nužno upravlja muž ili žena, nego da supružnici jedni drugima služe i zajedno donose odgovorne odluke za dobro obitelji. Biblijsko razumijevanje bračne odgovornosti uključuje uzajamnu brigu, poštovanje i ljubav, a odluke supružnika trebaju se oblikovati kroz strpljiv dijalog i zajedničko razlučivanje.
