magisterium.assessment_en: The message is largely aligned with the Catholic view of marriage because it links practical responsibility for family finances to capability rather than gender, and warns of the harm of irresponsible spending. Nevertheless, the expression that the woman should "take over management" should be understood within the framework of mutual conversation and responsible decision-making by the spouses, rather than as justification for unilateral control or the exclusion of the other.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic emphasis is not that finances must necessarily be managed by the husband or the wife, but that the spouses serve one another and together make responsible decisions for the good of the family. The biblical understanding of marital responsibility includes mutual care, respect, and love, and the decisions of the spouses should be shaped through patient dialogue and shared discernment.
concerns_en: The passage does not clarify whether the change in money management should be agreed upon; without such clarification, the phrase "let her manage" could be understood as unilateral decision-making.

The mention of the man as the "head" is not in itself elaborated enough to assess how the speaker understands that biblical image; it should not justify the neglect of mutual respect and responsibility.

sections.subtitle_en: Let the more capable one manage money, and it is no shame to seek help
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko sends the message that money should be managed by the more capable partner, regardless of whether that is the husband
sections.content_en:
Here Marko repeats the thought from the introductory clip. When one partner does not know how to manage money, let them leave it to the one who does. The common opinion is that the man is the leader and the head, but *"there are men who do not know how to manage money, and if the woman is more capable, give it to her so that she manages the money"*. If the husband persistently spends and rushes heedlessly, the solution is not for the wife to passively say *"he is the head, let him decide"*, but to take over management. *"Otherwise you will be in trouble."*

At a recent lecture on finances, he said: if it is constantly leaking away from you, if you are constantly in the red and in debt and "spinning from hollow to empty", **seek help**. *"That is no shame."* He advises talking to someone who will look at the situation from the outside and say what needs to be cut and put in order. The shame, he says, is being afraid to ask for help, not admitting that we do not know.

As an example, he cites an acquaintance who manages the wealth of **football players** and other wealthy people who do not know what to do with money. Having money does not mean being "the smartest in the world". The same applies at smaller levels: one can ask an expert or a friend who manages money well. One does not get out of debt overnight, because we did not find ourselves in it overnight either, so a plan and tactics are needed.

He also cites a sobering example of a **marriage that fell apart** while the spouses were in their twenties, after only a few years. One person knew nothing about finances and received only an allowance, and in the end, large debts and chaos emerged. *"It is a dangerous area"*, Marko concludes, and advises couples to talk and learn about money, *"because that is learned"*.

sections.subtitle: Financijski odgoj počinje džeparcem za užinu
sections.screenshot_description: Marko opisuje kako petogodišnjeg sina Jošuu uči raspoređivati novac
sections.content:
Krunoslav predlaže da se parovi financijama bave još prije braka, kroz programe i savjetovanja, jer se na zaručničkim tečajevima ta pitanja tek spomenu. Marko ide korak dalje: dobra priprema ne počinje prije braka, nego već **u osnovnoj školi**. Prvi susret s novcem je džeparac za užinu i tada treba naučiti raspolagati njime.

Opisuje kako to radi sa sinom **Jošuom**, koji ima pet godina. Kad Jošua dobije novac, otac ga uči da ga rasporedi: dio ostavlja za štednju, dio može pokloniti nekome kome treba pomoć, a 10 posto odvaja za **Eho Kids**. Program za djecu je besplatan, ali Marko mu objašnjava: *„Ajde, podrži program, odvoji te novce, to nisu tvoji novci.“* Jošua tako već sada uči koliko što vrijedi, koliko treba skupiti i koliko mu još fali u kasici.

Prepričava i video nekog milijardera koji je sinu davao tjedni džeparac i učio ga da dio štedi, dio donira, a ostatak troši. Kad ga je sin zamolio da mu kupi Coca-Colu, otac mu je rekao da je kupi sam. Kad je dječak vidio da stoji oko dva dolara, odustao je jer mu je bila preskupa. Iako je otac imao milijarde, želio je da sin nauči da raspolaže onim što ima i da ne može uvijek računati na očevu pomoć.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer novac prikazuje kao sredstvo kojim se uči odgovorno raspolagati, štedjeti i darivati, a financijski odgoj povezuje s obiteljskim odgojem. Ne tvrdi da štednja ili darivanje jamče materijalni uspjeh, niti da je bogatstvo samo po sebi cilj.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički pogled ne smatra novac sam po sebi zlim: važni su način njegova stjecanja i uporabe te spremnost da se njime služi bližnjemu; sveti Ćiril Jeruzalemski navodi da novac može postati sredstvom pomoći gladnima i siromašnima. Štednja zato može biti dio razboritog upravljanja dobrima, ali treba biti uravnotežena velikodušnošću i odgojem za krepost, a ne vezanošću uz imetak.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mostly aligned with Catholic teaching because it portrays money as a means by which one learns to manage responsibly, save, and give, and connects financial education with family upbringing. It does not claim that saving or giving guarantees material success, nor that wealth is an end in itself.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic view does not consider money evil in itself: what is important is the manner of its acquisition and use, as well as the readiness to serve one's neighbor with it; Saint Cyril of Jerusalem states that money can become a means of helping the hungry and the poor. Savings can therefore be part of the prudent administration of goods, but it should be balanced with generosity and formation for virtue, rather than attachment to possessions.

sections.subtitle_en: Financial education begins with pocket money for a snack
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko describes how he teaches his five-year-old son Jošua to allocate money
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav suggests that couples deal with finances even before marriage, through programs and counseling, because in marriage preparation courses these questions are only barely mentioned. Marko goes a step further: good preparation does not begin before marriage, but already **in elementary school**. The first encounter with money is pocket money for a snack, and that is when one should learn how to manage it.

He describes how he does this with his son **Jošua**, who is five years old. When Jošua gets money, his father teaches him to allocate it: he leaves a portion for savings, a portion he can give to someone who needs help, and he sets aside 10 percent for **Eho Kids**. The children's program is free, but Marko explains to him: *“Come on, support the program, set that money aside, that is not your money.”* Jošua is thus already learning how much something is worth, how much he needs to collect, and how much he is still missing in his piggy bank.

He also recounts a video of a billionaire who gave his son weekly pocket money and taught him to save a portion, donate a portion, and spend the rest. When the son asked him to buy him a Coca-Cola, the father told him to buy it himself. When the boy saw that it cost around two dollars, he gave up because it was too expensive for him. Although the father had billions, he wanted his son to learn to manage what he has and that he cannot always count on his father's help.

sections.subtitle: Razgovor o novcu prije oltara
sections.screenshot_description: Marko prepričava Mirjaninu zabrinutost zbog načina trošenja prije braka
sections.content:
Za one koji takvo znanje nisu stekli u djetinjstvu Marko ima jasan savjet: o novcu treba razgovarati **prije braka**. Kao primjer navodi vlastito iskustvo. Prije vjenčanja bilo je nekoliko situacija u kojima je Mirjana bila zabrinuta kako će se postaviti zbog jedne obiteljske situacije vezane uz trošenje novca.

Rekla mu je: *„Sve pet, mi sad nismo u braku, ali mene brine misliš li ti da je to okej, taj način trošenja? Jer kasnije ćemo mi biti skupa, i ako je tebi ovo okej, onda imamo problem.“* Marko je tada morao jasno razdvojiti vlastite stavove od obiteljskih navika i pratiti kako se postavlja.

Tim primjerom zatvara se blok o financijama u braku. Marko je spomenuo davanje desetine i darivanje, što je Krunoslavu poslužilo kao prijelaz na sljedeće pitanje.

magisterium.assessment: Savjet da zaručnici prije braka otvoreno razgovaraju o novcu i navikama trošenja uglavnom je usklađen s katoličkim razumijevanjem priprave za brak: takav razgovor može pomoći da razborito razluče očekivanja i moguće poteškoće. Odlomak ne iznosi tvrdnju koja bi proturječila katoličkom nauku ili Svetom pismu.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva potiče zaručnike da prije ženidbe razgovaraju o svojim očekivanjima i životu koji žele graditi zajedno, jer međusobna privlačnost sama po sebi nije dovoljna za postojan bračni savez. Takav razgovor o novcu može biti dio šire priprave obilježene dijalogom, molitvom i kršćanskim vrijednostima, a ne usredotočenošću na bogatstvo ili privid.

citations.document_title: Preparation for the sacrament of marriage

magisterium.assessment_en: The advice that engaged couples should speak openly about money and spending habits before marriage is largely aligned with the Catholic understanding of marriage preparation: such a conversation can help them prudently discern expectations and possible difficulties. The passage does not make any claim that would contradict Catholic teaching or Sacred Scripture.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church encourages engaged couples to talk about their expectations and the life they want to build together before marriage, because mutual attraction in itself is not sufficient for an enduring marital covenant. Such a conversation about money can be part of a broader preparation marked by dialogue, prayer, and Christian values, rather than a focus on wealth or appearance.

sections.subtitle_en: A Conversation about Money before the Altar
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko recounts Mirjana's concern about spending habits before marriage
sections.content_en:
For those who did not acquire such knowledge in childhood, Marko has clear advice: money should be discussed **before marriage**. As an example, he cites his own experience. Before the wedding, there were several situations in which Mirjana was worried about how he would position himself regarding a family situation related to spending money.

She told him: *"All good, we are not married now, but I'm worried whether you think that's okay, that way of spending? Because later we will be together, and if this is okay with you, then we have a problem."* Marko then had to clearly separate his own attitudes from family habits and monitor how he positioned himself.

With that example, the block on finances in marriage closes. Marko mentioned tithing and giving, which served Krunoslav as a transition to the next question.

sections.subtitle: „Iskušajte me”: desetina kao jedino mjesto gdje Bog dopušta da ga se kuša
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj Krunoslav citira proroka Malahiju i otvara temu desetine
sections.content:
Drugi dio razgovora otvara pitanje koje se u katoličkim krugovima rijetko postavlja naglas. Voditelj **Krunoslav** primjećuje da se Marko Matijašević u prethodnom odgovoru već dotaknuo desetine, opisujući kako svog sina uči da odvaja 10% za program Echo Kids. Krunoslav zatim pita kakav bi trebao biti stav katolika prema desetini. Upozorava da se vjernici tom temom vrlo malo bave i vrlo malo daruju. Razumije da mnogi imaju financijskih problema, pa se grčevito drže iznosa koji imaju.

Krunoslav dodaje osobnu crtu. Tog je dana naišao na citat iz knjige proroka Malahije, koji slobodno parafrazira: *„Ako želiš iskušati Gospodina, daj desetinu i vidi što će On učiniti.”* Svjedoči da on i supruga izdvajaju desetinu i da im se ona **mnogostruko vraća**. Ponekad to zaborave jer rješavaju druge stvari, ali ipak vide koliko ih Bog blagoslivlja kad daju od onoga što im je povjerio na upravljanje.

Marko Matijašević nadovezuje se na isti tekst i ističe njegovu posebnost. Prema njegovim riječima, desetina je **jedina stvar u Bibliji za koju Bog kaže da ga smijemo kušati**. Vjernici znaju zapovijed *„Ne kušaj Boga svoga”*, a ovdje stoji suprotno: *„Kušajte me, dajte prvine u moju riznicu i onda me iskušajte neću li onda izlit blagoslov na vas.”* Gost otkriva da je i sam tog dana nekome slao baš taj citat. Zaključuje da vjernik na tom području doslovno ima Božje dopuštenje da ga iskuša, pa se pita zašto to ne prihvatiti.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na velikodušnom darivanju i upravljanju dobrima može biti u skladu s katoličkim pozivom na zahvalnost, milostinju i potporu crkvenom djelovanju. Ipak, iz dostupnog sažetka nije moguće procijeniti cijelu izlaganu argumentaciju, a tvrdnju da je desetina jedino mjesto gdje Bog dopušta da ga se kuša treba ograničiti na konkretan odlomak Malahije, ne pretvoriti u opće pravilo ili obećanje financijskog dobitka.
concerns: Malahija 3,10 doista sadrži Božji poziv: „stavite me na kušnju” u vezi s prinošenjem pune desetine u spremište hrama, ali tekst govori u posebnom kontekstu Izraelova Saveza, hrama i uzdržavanja doma Božjega; sam po sebi ne uspostavlja obvezu da svaki katolik daje točno deset posto niti da će zauzvrat dobiti materijalno blagostanje.

Ako se poruka shvati kao da je davanje desetine nužan uvjet za Božji blagoslov ili način da se od Boga iznudi financijska nagrada, to bi zamaglilo kršćansko shvaćanje dara i providnosti. Dostupni sažetak ne potvrđuje da podcast izričito zastupa takav stav, pa je riječ o mogućoj nejasnoći, a ne sigurnom zaključku.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički naglasak nije na mehaničkom postotku nego na odgovornom i velikodušnom raspolaganju dobrima koja se promatraju kao povjerena upraviteljima; crkveni nauk ističe njihovu namjenu za opće dobro, osobito za siromašne i potrebne. Povijesni katolički izvori potiču razuman udio za potrebe Crkve, a sv. Ivan Zlatousti preporučuje desetinu kao duhovnu disciplinu, ali izričito kaže da je ne propisuje kao zakon. Zato se Malahijin poziv može primijeniti kao poticaj povjerenju i vjernosti, uz slobodu i razboritost te bez obećavanja zajamčenog materijalnog povrata.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on generous giving and stewardship of goods can be in accordance with the Catholic call to gratitude, almsgiving, and support of the Church's activity. However, from the available summary it is not possible to evaluate the entire argumentation presented, and the claim that the tithe is the only place where God allows Himself to be tested should be limited to the specific passage of Malachi, not turned into a general rule or a promise of financial gain.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic emphasis is not on a mechanical percentage, but on the responsible and generous disposal of goods that are viewed as entrusted to stewards; Church teaching highlights their purpose for the common good, especially for the poor and needy. Historical Catholic sources encourage a reasonable share for the needs of the Church, and St. John Chrysostom recommends the tithe as a spiritual discipline, but explicitly says he does not prescribe it as a law. Therefore, Malachi's call can be applied as an encouragement to trust and fidelity, with freedom and prudence, and without promising a guaranteed material return.
concerns_en: Malachi 3:10 indeed contains God's invitation: "put me to the test" regarding bringing the full tithe into the temple storehouse, but the text speaks in the specific context of Israel's Covenant, the temple, and the maintenance of the house of God; in itself, it does not establish an obligation for every Catholic to give exactly ten percent, nor that one will receive material prosperity in return.

If the message is understood as though giving a tithe were a necessary condition for God's blessing or a way to extort a financial reward from God, this would obscure the Christian understanding of gift and providence. The available summary does not confirm that the podcast explicitly advocates such a position, so this is a matter of potential ambiguity rather than a definitive conclusion.

sections.subtitle_en: "Test me": the tithe as the only place where God allows Himself to be tested
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host Krunoslav quotes the prophet Malachi and opens the topic of the tithe
sections.content_en:
The second part of the conversation opens a question that is rarely asked aloud in Catholic circles. Host **Krunoslav** notes that Marko Matijašević already touched upon the tithe in his previous answer, describing how he teaches his son to set aside 10% for the Echo Kids program. Krunoslav then asks what a Catholic's attitude toward the tithe should be. He warns that the faithful engage very little with this topic and give very little. He understands that many have financial problems, so they cling tightly to the amount they have.

Krunoslav adds a personal note. That day, he came across a quote from the Book of the Prophet Malachi, which he freely paraphrases: *"If you want to test the Lord, give the tithe and see what He will do."* He testifies that he and his wife set aside the tithe and that it **returns to them manifold**. Sometimes they forget to do so because they are dealing with other things, but they still see how much God blesses them when they give from what He has entrusted to their stewardship.

Marko Matijašević builds on the same text and highlights its uniqueness. According to him, the tithe is **the only thing in the Bible about which God says we may test Him**. The faithful know the commandment *"Do not put your God to the test"*, yet here stands the opposite: *"Test me, bring the full tithes into the storehouse, and see if I will not then pour down a blessing upon you."* The guest reveals that he himself had sent that exact quote to someone that very day. He concludes that in this area a believer literally has God's permission to test Him, so he asks why not accept it.

sections.subtitle: Zašto Crkva šuti o novcu i zašto vjersko ne mora biti besplatno
sections.screenshot_description: Marko Matijašević objašnjava zašto se u Crkvi izbjegava tema financija
sections.content:
Marko Matijašević smatra da se o desetini šuti zato što se **u Crkvi općenito slabo govori o financijama**. Ljudi su na tom području već povrijeđeni i uglavnom imaju negativan stav prema toj temi. Zato razumije svećenike koji se ustručavaju o tome govoriti, jer od vjernika često čuju reakciju: *„Nemoj mi još s tim i u crkvi.”*

Iz toga proizlazi problem s kojim se njegova udruga Eho često susreće. Postoji očekivanje da sve što je vjersko mora biti besplatno, kao da ništa ne vrijedi i treba se samo dijeliti. Gost navodi tipičan prigovor: *„Ne mogu vjerovati da naplaćujete čitanje Božje riječi.”* Odgovara da se to ne naplaćuje. Svatko si može kupiti Bibliju i čitati je sam. Ono što se plaća jest sve ostalo:

- **uloženo vrijeme** i trud organizatora,
- **tehnika i oprema**,
- sadržaj koji posjetitelj dobiva „serviran”, a kojem se netko posvetio kroz mnogo sati rada.

Matijašević tvrdi da oni koji vjernicima prešućuju ovu temu iz obzira prema njihovoj povrijeđenosti ne čine im uslugu. Time im, kaže, propuštaju objasniti koji blagoslov donosi davanje i što Bog misli o financijama.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak opisuje otpor prema razgovoru o novcu, što samo po sebi nije u suprotnosti s katoličkim naukom: Crkva ima stvarne materijalne potrebe, a vjernici su pozvani pomagati ih. Ipak, iz nedovršene rečenice nije moguće utvrditi kako govornik razgraničuje opravdano financiranje službi i organizacije od nedopuštene komercijalizacije sakramenata.
concerns: Ako se tvrdnja da vjersko ne mora biti besplatno shvati kao opravdanje za naplaćivanje sakramenata ili uvjetovanje pastoralne službe tarifom, to bi bilo protivno crkvenom upozorenju da se sakramentalni život ne komercijalizira. Dostupni odlomak ne pokazuje da govornik doista zastupa takvo stajalište.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk istodobno drži da je navještaj evanđelja dar koji se ne smije pretvoriti u robu i da zajednica treba materijalna sredstva za bogoslužje, apostolat, karitativni rad i dostojno uzdržavanje službenika. Zato je važno razlikovati slobodan dar i dobrovoljni prilog za potrebe Crkve od cijene koja bi sakrament učinila uvjetovanom uslugom; vjernici su pozvani pridonositi prema svojim mogućnostima i u duhu solidarnosti.

citations.document_title: Instruction "The pastoral conversion of the Parish community in the service of the evangelising mission of the Church", of the Congregation for the Clergy, 20.07.2020

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage describes resistance to talking about money, which in itself is not contrary to Catholic teaching: the Church has real material needs, and the faithful are called to help them. Nevertheless, from the incomplete sentence it is not possible to determine how the speaker distinguishes the justified financing of ministries and organization from the illicit commercialization of the sacraments.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching simultaneously holds that the proclamation of the Gospel is a gift that must not be turned into a commodity and that the community needs material means for worship, apostolate, charitable work, and the worthy maintenance of ministers. Therefore, it is important to distinguish a free gift and a voluntary contribution for the needs of the Church from a price that would make a sacrament a conditional service; the faithful are called to contribute according to their abilities and in a spirit of solidarity.
concerns_en: If the assertion that what is religious does not have to be free is understood as a justification for charging for sacraments or conditioning pastoral ministry on a tariff, that would be contrary to the Church's warning not to commercialize sacramental life. The available passage does not show that the speaker actually advocates such a position.

sections.subtitle_en: Why the Church is silent about money and why what is religious does not have to be free
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko Matijašević explains why the topic of finances is avoided in the Church
sections.content_en:
Marko Matijašević believes that there is silence about the tithe because **in the Church, finances are generally rarely spoken about**. People are already hurt in that area and mostly have a negative attitude toward that topic. Therefore, he understands priests who hesitate to speak about it, because they often hear a reaction from the faithful: *„Don't come to me with that in church as well.”*

From this stems the problem that his association udruga Eho often encounters. There is an expectation that everything religious must be free, as if it is worth nothing and should only be handed out. The guest cites a typical objection: *„I cannot believe that you charge for reading the Word of God.”* He replies that this is not charged for. Anyone can buy a Bible and read it themselves. What is paid for is everything else:

- **invested time** and effort of the organizers,
- **technology and equipment**,
- content that the visitor receives „served”, to which someone devoted themselves through many hours of work.

Matijašević claims that those who keep silent about this topic before the faithful out of consideration for their hurt do not do them a favor. In doing so, he says, they fail to explain to them what blessing giving brings and what God thinks about finances.

sections.subtitle: Desetina nije milostinja: Tobijinih 30 posto i sedam židovskih davanja
sections.screenshot_description: Gost razlikuje desetinu od milostinje na primjeru Tobije
sections.content:
Jedna od ključnih poanti epizode jest razlika koju vjernici često ne prave. Matijašević kaže da je davanje milostinje ili donacija za humanitarnu svrhu za većinu ljudi normalna stvar. **To, međutim, nije desetina.** Po njegovu tumačenju, desetina je namijenjena isključivo **evangelizaciji i izgradnji hrama**: ide Bogu, onima koji mu služe i širenju vjere. *„Pomoć prijatelju u nevolji nije desetina”*, naglašava.

Kao ilustraciju vraća se Tobiji, kojeg je spomenuo na početku razgovora kad je govorio o temeljima udruge Eho. Prema gostu, Tobija je davao čak **30% svojih primanja**:

- **10%** za hram,
- **10%** kao milostinju,
- **10%** trošio je kod svojih sunarodnjaka, kupujući njihove proizvode i potičući njihovo gospodarstvo.

Matijašević dodaje širi kontekst. Židovi su poznavali oko **sedam vrsta davanja**, uključujući razne žrtve i paljenice, a desetina je bila samo jedna od njih. Danas, kaže, dovoljno je spomenuti samo desetinu pa nastaje *„plač i škrgut zuba”*. Tema je osjetljiva upravo zbog te povrijeđenosti, a o blagoslovu koji ona nosi govori se premalo.

magisterium.assessment: Razlikovanje desetine od milostinje može biti korisno, a davanje za uzdržavanje službenika Crkve i njezino poslanje ima biblijske i katoličke temelje. Ipak, tvrdnja da je desetina namijenjena isključivo evangelizaciji i izgradnji hrama te da pomoć potrebitima nije povezana s njom pretjerano je uska i ne odgovara prikazu desetina u Tobitovoj knjizi.
concerns: Tobit izričito navodi da je treću desetinu davao siročadi, udovicama i pridošlicama koje su prihvatile izraelsku vjeru, pa se iz njegova primjera ne može zaključiti da desetina služi isključivo hramu, službenicima i evangelizaciji.

U Tobitovu prikazu postoje različite namjene: prinosi svećenicima i levitima, druga desetina povezana s odlaskom u Jeruzalem te treća namijenjena ranjivim skupinama. Zato je kategorička tvrdnja da pomoć prijatelju u nevolji ne može biti desetina teološki neprecizna, iako se konkretna pomoć može razlikovati od redovitog davanja za uzdržavanje službe ili zajednice.

Katoličko učenje ne dopušta da se davanje za Crkvu postavi kao zamjena za dužnost pomaganja siromašnima: kršćanska dobra imaju društvenu namjenu, a pomoć potrebitima može biti dužnost pravde i ljubavi.
magisterium.enrichment: Tobitova knjiga povezuje vjernost Bogu s različitim oblicima davanja: uz prinose za svećenike i levite, Tobit navodi i darove siročadi, udovicama i pridošlicama. Katolički kontekst zato razlikuje svrhe i oblike darivanja, ali ne suprotstavlja potporu crkvenom poslanju djelima milosrđa: Tobit poziva da se ne okreće lice od siromaha, a Benedikt XVI. opisuje pomoć potrebitima kao dužnost pravde prije nego kao čin ljubavi.

The Holy Bible (The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)), Tobit 4
Message of His Holiness Benedict XVI for Lent 2008

magisterium.assessment_en: Distinguishing the tithe from almsgiving can be useful, and giving for the support of Church ministers and its mission has biblical and Catholic foundations. Nevertheless, the claim that the tithe is intended exclusively for evangelization and the building of the temple and that helping those in need is not connected with it is overly narrow and does not correspond to the presentation of tithes in the Book of Tobit.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Book of Tobit connects faithfulness to God with various forms of giving: alongside offerings for priests and Levites, Tobit also cites gifts to orphans, widows, and strangers. The Catholic context therefore distinguishes the purposes and forms of giving, but does not oppose support for the ecclesial mission to works of mercy: Tobit calls for not turning one's face away from the poor, and Benedict XVI describes helping the needy as a duty of justice before being an act of charity.
concerns_en: Tobit explicitly states that he gave the third tithe to orphans, widows, and strangers who had accepted the Israelite faith, so it cannot be concluded from his example that the tithe serves exclusively the temple, ministers, and evangelization.

In Tobit's presentation, there are different purposes: offerings to priests and Levites, a second tithe connected with traveling to Jerusalem, and a third intended for vulnerable groups. Therefore, the categorical claim that helping a friend in need cannot be a tithe is theologically imprecise, although concrete help may differ from regular giving for the support of ministry or the community.

Catholic teaching does not permit giving to the Church to be established as a substitute for the duty of helping the poor: Christian goods have a social destination, and helping the needy can be a duty of justice and charity.

sections.subtitle_en: Tithe Is Not Almsgiving: Tobit's 30 Percent and Seven Jewish Offerings
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest distinguishes the tithe from almsgiving using the example of Tobit
sections.content_en:
One of the key points of the episode is the distinction that believers often do not make. Matijašević says that giving alms or donations for a humanitarian purpose is a normal thing for most people. **That, however, is not a tithe.** According to his interpretation, the tithe is intended exclusively for **evangelization and the building of the temple**: it goes to God, to those who serve Him, and to the spreading of the faith. *“Helping a friend in need is not a tithe,”* he emphasizes.

As an illustration, he returns to Tobit, whom he mentioned at the beginning of the conversation when speaking about the foundations of the association Eho. According to the guest, Tobit gave as much as **30% of his income**:

- **10%** for the temple,
- **10%** as alms,
- **10%** he spent among his compatriots, buying their products and stimulating their economy.

Matijašević adds a broader context. The Jews recognized about **seven types of offerings**, including various sacrifices and burnt offerings, and the tithe was only one of them. Today, he says, it is enough just to mention the tithe and there is *“weeping and gnashing of teeth.”* The topic is sensitive precisely because of that hurt, and too little is said about the blessing it brings.

sections.subtitle: Novi zavjet ne ukida desetinu: ljubav ide iznad zakona, a ne ispod njega
sections.screenshot_description: Marko Matijašević objašnjava da ljubav nadilazi zakon
sections.content:
Matijašević se zatim osvrće na čest prigovor. Mnogi se pozivaju na Novi zavjet, u kojem Pavao kaže da svatko daje *„kako je srcem odlučio”* jer *„Bog ljubi vesela darivatelja”*. Iz toga zaključuju da desetina više ne vrijedi.

Gost na to odgovara dvama argumentima. Prvo, **Novi zavjet nije ukinuo Stari zavjet**. Drugo, desetina doista jest zakon, ali **ljubav ide iznad zakona**. Ako zakon traži 10%, onda bi ljubav trebala dati više: *„Inače nema ljubavi. Ako ja odrađujem samo ono što moram, to je zakon.”* Odbacuje tumačenje u kojem ljubav znači ukidanje zakona, svedeno na pristup *„sola gratia”* u kojem je sve oprošteno i *„sve divno i krasno”*.

Poziva se i na Pavlove riječi: *„Tko sije oskudno, oskudno će i žeti.”* Ne može se, kaže, sijati oskudno i očekivati blagoslov.

Gost predviđa i sljedeći prigovor: netko ima novca, ne daje desetinu, a ipak izgleda blagoslovljeno. Odgovor mu je jasan: **količina novca na računu ne govori o blagoslovu**. *„Ti možeš imati milijune i biti proklet”*, kaže. Izjednačavanje bogatstva i blagoslova pripisuje teologiji prosperiteta, a ne kršćanskom razumijevanju blagoslova.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak dobro naglašava da kršćanska velikodušnost ne bi smjela biti tek hladno ispunjavanje minimuma te da Novi zavjet poziva na radosno darivanje. Ipak, tvrdnja da Novi zavjet nije ukinuo Stari zavjet ostaje teološki neprecizna ako se iz nje izvodi da je desetina od 10% i dalje obvezujući zakon za sve kršćane ili da je davanje ispod tog iznosa znak nedostatka ljubavi.
concerns: Potrebno je razlikovati trajnu vrijednost Starog zavjeta od obveze kršćana da slijede svaku odredbu Mojsijeva zakona: kršćansko čitanje govori o ispunjenju i preoblikovanju zakona u Kristu, a ne o nepromijenjenoj primjeni svih njegovih propisa.

Odlomak ne daje osnovu za zaključak da je točno desetina univerzalna novozavjetna obveza niti da je darivanje manje od 10% samo po sebi manjak ljubavi. Pavao naglašava darivanje prema osobnoj odluci, bez prisile; kršćanska velikodušnost ne treba se svesti ni na zakonski minimum ni na pritisak da se mora dati više.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao povezuje darežljivost s radošću i slobodom, a istodobno potiče vjernike da svojim obiljem pomognu onima koji oskudijevaju; riječ je o velikodušnosti koja uzima u obzir potrebe drugih i mogućnosti darivatelja. Stoga se desetina može promatrati kao povijesni i duhovni poticaj na predanje dobara Bogu i služenje zajednici, ali navedeni tekstovi ne potvrđuju da je baš 10% obvezna novozavjetna norma.

citations.document_title: Eternal Life: A Merited Free Gift?
The Holy Bible (The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)), 2 Corinthians 9:7
Sermon 17 of St. Leo the Great (Pope Leo I (Leo the Great))
On the Unity of the Two Testaments: In What Sense Is the Torah a Law for Christians?

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage rightly emphasizes that Christian generosity should not be merely a cold fulfillment of the minimum and that the New Testament calls for joyful giving. Nevertheless, the claim that the New Testament did not abolish the Old Testament remains theologically imprecise if it is deduced from it that the 10% tithe is still a binding law for all Christians or that giving below that amount is a sign of a lack of love.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul links generosity with joy and freedom, while at the same time encouraging believers to help those in need with their abundance; it is a generosity that takes into account the needs of others and the abilities of the giver. Therefore, the tithe can be seen as a historical and spiritual impulse for surrendering goods to God and serving the community, but the cited texts do not confirm that 10% specifically is an obligatory New Testament norm.
concerns_en: It is necessary to distinguish the enduring value of the Old Testament from the obligation of Christians to follow every precept of the Mosaic Law: a Christian reading speaks of the fulfillment and transformation of the law in Christ, rather than the unchanged application of all its precepts.

The passage provides no basis for concluding that the tithe is strictly a universal New Testament obligation or that giving less than 10% is in itself a lack of love. Paul emphasizes giving according to personal decision, without compulsion; Christian generosity should not be reduced either to a legal minimum or to pressure that one must give more.

sections.subtitle_en: The New Testament does not abolish the tithe: love goes above the law, not below it
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko Matijašević explains that love transcends the law
sections.content_en:
Matijašević then addresses a common objection. Many appeal to the New Testament, in which Paul says that each one gives *“as he has decided in his heart”* because *“God loves a cheerful giver”*. From this they conclude that the tithe no longer applies.

The guest responds to this with two arguments. First, **the New Testament did not abolish the Old Testament**. Second, the tithe indeed is a law, but **love goes above the law**. If the law demands 10%, then love should give more: *“Otherwise there is no love. If I only do what I have to do, that is the law.”* He rejects the interpretation in which love means the abolition of the law, reduced to a *“sola gratia”* approach in which everything is forgiven and *“everything is wonderful and great”*.

He also refers to Paul's words: *“Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly.”* One cannot, he says, sow sparingly and expect a blessing.

The guest also anticipates the next objection: someone has money, does not give a tithe, and yet looks blessed. His answer is clear: **the amount of money in the account does not speak of blessing**. *“You can have millions and be cursed,”* he says. Equating wealth and blessing he attributes to prosperity theology, and not to the Christian understanding of blessing.

sections.subtitle: Udovičin novčić i tri eura koja vrijede koliko tuđih sto
sections.screenshot_description: Gost prepričava prispodobu o udovici koja je dala sve što je imala
sections.content:
Kako bi pokazao što je Bogu doista važno, Matijašević podsjeća na događaj u hramu. Isus pita učenike tko je dao najviše dok bogati ubacuju svoje kese, a jedna žena tek nekoliko novčića. Njegov je odgovor da je dala upravo ona, jer su drugi davali od viška, a ona je dala sve što je imala.

Pouka koju gost izvodi glasi: **iz Božje perspektive nije stvar u iznosu**. Ljudima zato poručuje: *„Pa daj ti tri eura.”* Ako je to nečiji trenutni maksimum, to vrijedi jednako kao nečijih sto. Važno je biti vjeran i povjerovati Bogu.

Matijašević dijeli i osobno iskustvo. Od prvog novca koji je zaradio uvijek je izdvajao desetinu, a svjedočanstva koja iz toga ima opisuje kao **ogromna iskustva Božje providnosti**. Posebno naglašava da o tome ne govori radi vlastite koristi: *„Ja neću biti suđen za tvoj dio, ja ću biti za svoj dio. Ti ćeš biti suđen što si napravio s onime što imaš.”*

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje je uglavnom usklađeno: Isus doista vrednuje udovičin dar prema njezinu siromaštvu i potpunoj predanosti, a ne samo prema nominalnom iznosu (Mk 12,41–44; Lk 21,1–4). Ipak, tvrdnja da iz Božje perspektive „nije stvar u iznosu” traži pojašnjenje kako se ne bi shvatila kao da su iznos, stvarne potrebe darivatelja ili razborita odgovornost nevažni.
concerns: U Markovu tekstu Isus ne pita učenike tko je dao najviše; on promatra darove, a zatim poučava učenike da je udovica dala više, jer je darovala iz siromaštva sve što joj je bilo za život (Mk 12,41–44). To je neznatna pojedinost u prepričavanju, ali vrijedi je ispraviti.

Poziv „Pa daj ti tri eura” može biti dobar primjer darivanja prema vlastitim mogućnostima, ali bez dodatnog konteksta može zvučati kao pritisak na osobu koja je u oskudici. Isusov primjer ne bi trebalo pretvoriti u zahtjev da svatko daje sve što ima ili u obećanje da će novčani dar donijeti financijski blagoslov.
magisterium.enrichment: Isus uspoređuje darove: bogati daju od obilja, a udovica od siromaštva daje sve što ima za život; naglasak je na njezinoj velikodušnosti i predanju, a ne na propisanom iznosu koji bi svatko morao dati (Mk 12,41–44; Lk 21,1–4). Benedikt XVI. opisuje njezin dar kao darivanje cijele sebe te ističe da se konkretno darivanje razlikuje prema mogućnostima i životnim okolnostima pojedinca. Zato je primjereno poticati nesebičnost, ali i izbjeći manipuliranje savješću ili predstavljanje darivanja kao jamstva materijalne dobiti.
magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation is generally aligned: Jesus indeed values the widow's gift according to her poverty and total commitment, not merely according to the nominal amount (Mk 12:41–44; Lk 21:1–4). Nevertheless, the assertion that from God's perspective “it is not about the amount” requires clarification so that it is not understood as meaning that the amount, the actual needs of the giver, or prudent responsibility are unimportant.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus compares the gifts: the rich give out of abundance, while the widow out of poverty gives everything she has to live on; the emphasis is on her generosity and surrender, not on a prescribed amount that everyone would have to give (Mk 12:41–44; Lk 21:1–4). Benedict XVI describes her gift as the giving of her entire self and points out that concrete giving differs according to the possibilities and life circumstances of the individual. Therefore, it is appropriate to encourage selflessness, but also to avoid manipulating conscience or presenting giving as a guarantee of material gain.
concerns_en: In Mark's text, Jesus does not ask the disciples who gave the most; he observes the gifts and then teaches the disciples that the widow gave more, because out of poverty she gave everything she had to live on (Mk 12:41–44). This is a minor detail in the retelling, but it is worth correcting.

The appeal “Well, give three euros then” can be a good example of giving according to one's own means, but without additional context it can sound like pressure on a person who is in need. Jesus' example should not be turned into a demand that everyone give everything they have or into a promise that a monetary gift will bring financial blessing.

sections.subtitle_en: The widow's mite and three euros that are worth as much as someone else's hundred
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest retells the parable of the widow who gave everything she had
sections.content_en:
In order to show what is truly important to God, Matijašević recalls the event in the temple. Jesus asks the disciples who gave the most while the rich throw in their bags, and a woman just a few coins. His answer is that she gave the most, because others gave out of their surplus, while she gave everything she had.

The lesson the guest draws is: **from God's perspective, it is not about the amount**. He therefore tells people: *“Well, give three euros then.”* If that is someone's current maximum, it is worth just as much as someone else's hundred. It is important to be faithful and trust God.

Matijašević also shares a personal experience. From the first money he earned, he always set aside a tithe, and he describes the testimonies he has from this as **immense experiences of God's providence**. He especially emphasizes that he is not speaking about this for his own gain: *“I will not be judged for your share, I will be judged for my share. You will be judged for what you did with what you have.”*

sections.subtitle: Samo vjernik daje za evangelizaciju: protestanti, kalež od dijamanta i stare stolice
sections.screenshot_description: Matijašević uspoređuje katolike i protestante te govori o kaležu
sections.content:
Matijašević ističe razliku između humanitarnog davanja i davanja za evangelizaciju. **Za humanitarnu svrhu dat će svatko**, pa i nevjernik kad vidi veliku potrebu. Za evangelizaciju će dati samo vjernik, jer nevjerniku ona ništa ne znači.

U tome vidi i razlog zašto su protestanti na Zapadu, kako kaže, uspješniji od katolika. Za protestante je davanje desetine i ulaganje u evangelizaciju sasvim normalna stvar. Katolici bi, prema njegovim riječima, najradije da sve bude *„štalica”*, pa se odmah pitaju zašto je sve u crkvi tako skupo.

Gost misli drukčije: *„Pa nek budu skupe stvari.”* Kao primjer uzima **kalež**. U njemu je krv Kristova koja je spasila vjernika, pa neka bude i od dijamanta, umjesto obične šalice za koju neki misle da je dovoljna.

Prepričava i anegdotu jednog propovjednika koji je uređivao molitvenu dvoranu. Ljudi su mu nudili stolice koje im kod kuće više ne trebaju, a on je uzvratio pitanjem: *„Te stolice nisu dovoljno dobre za tvoju kuću, a dovoljno su dobre za Božji dom?”* U dvoranu su na kraju stavljene nove stolice. Razlog je, kaže Matijašević, to što **Bog zaslužuje najbolje** i što takav odnos pokazuje koliko je čovjeku stalo.

Na kraju poglavlja poziva se na proroka **Hagaja**. Narod je izgradio svoje kuće, a Božji dom zaboravio. Zato *„sipaju u kesu, a prosipa im se”* i siju, a ne žanju. Blagoslov u vlastitim kesama dolazi kad se počne graditi Božji dom.

magisterium.assessment: Ispravno je naglašeno da evangelizacija treba materijalnu potporu te da vjernici imaju posebnu odgovornost sudjelovati u poslanju Crkve, ali tvrdnja da će za evangelizaciju dati samo vjernik previše je kategorična: Crkva poziva i ljude dobre volje da je podupru. Usporedba protestanata i katolika kao skupina te zaključak da je razlika u uspješnosti posljedica davanja desetine nisu potkrijepljeni prikazanim odlomkom, a njegov je završetak prekinut pa se ne može procijeniti puna poanta o uređenju crkve.
concerns: Tvrdnja da nevjerniku evangelizacija ništa ne znači generalizira motive ljudi: netko tko ne dijeli vjeru može ipak poduprijeti misijsko djelovanje iz dobre volje ili poštovanja prema njegovu društvenom doprinosu. Papinsko učenje izričito govori o prikupljanju pomoći od ljudi dobre volje za misijsko poslanje Crkve.
Katolički vjernici pozvani su surađivati u evangelizaciji prema svojim mogućnostima, ali iz toga ne slijedi da samo vjernici mogu ili hoće financijski pridonositi.

Odlomak izjednačuje protestantsko davanje desetine s uspjehom u evangelizaciji, no prikazani izvori ne potkrepljuju tu usporedbu ni uzročnu vezu. Ne treba iznositi takav zaključak bez dodatnih dokaza, a davanje u kršćanskom smislu treba biti slobodno i ne pod prisilom.

Kritika ideje da sve u crkvi mora biti poput „štalice” može upozoriti na pretjerano odbacivanje materijalne skrbi za bogoslužje; ipak, budući da je rečenica prekinuta, nije jasno kritizira li govornik siromašan izgled kao takav ili nešto drugo. Crkveni prostor i bogoslužje zahtijevaju sredstva, ali opravdanost pojedinog troška ne proizlazi automatski iz te opće potrebe.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko učenje drži da materijalno pomaganje misijama može služiti i navještaju Evanđelja i djelima ljubavi; ta se poslanja ne trebaju postavljati jedno nasuprot drugome. Sveti Pavao traži da se daje dobrovoljno, prema odluci srca, a ne „pod prisilom”, pa se velikodušnost ne može svesti na obvezni postotak ili mjerilo vjere. Istodobno, dostojanstvo bogoslužja i održavanje crkvenih ustanova legitimne su potrebe, koje treba razborito uravnotežiti s brigom za siromašne i misijsko djelovanje.

citations.document_title: The Holy Bible (The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)), 2 Corinthians 9
The Holy Bible (The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)), Nehemiah 10

magisterium.assessment_en: It is correctly emphasized that evangelization needs material support and that believers have a special responsibility to participate in the mission of the Church, but the claim that only a believer will give for evangelization is too categorical: the Church also invites people of goodwill to support it. The comparison of Protestants and Catholics as groups and the conclusion that the difference in success is a consequence of tithing are not supported by the presented passage, and its ending is cut off so the full point about furnishing the church cannot be assessed.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching holds that materially assisting missions can serve both the proclamation of the Gospel and works of charity; these missions should not be set against each other. Saint Paul requires that one give voluntarily, according to the decision of the heart, and not "under compulsion," so generosity cannot be reduced to an obligatory percentage or a measure of faith. At the same time, the dignity of divine worship and the maintenance of church institutions are legitimate needs, which should be prudently balanced with care for the poor and missionary activity.
concerns_en: The claim that evangelization means nothing to an unbeliever generalizes people's motives: someone who does not share the faith may still support missionary activity out of goodwill or respect for its social contribution. Papal teaching explicitly speaks of collecting aid from people of goodwill for the Church's missionary mission.
Catholic believers are called to cooperate in evangelization according to their abilities, but it does not follow from this that only believers can or will contribute financially.

The passage equates Protestant tithing with success in evangelization, but the presented sources do not support that comparison or causal connection. Such a conclusion should not be drawn without additional evidence, and giving in the Christian sense must be free and not under compulsion.

The criticism of the idea that everything in the church must be like a „little stable” may point out an excessive rejection of material care for divine worship; nevertheless, since the sentence is interrupted, it is not clear whether the speaker is criticizing an impoverished appearance as such or something else. Church space and worship require resources, but the justification of an individual expense does not automatically follow from that general need.

sections.subtitle_en: Only a believer gives for evangelization: Protestants, a chalice of diamonds, and old chairs
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matijašević compares Catholics and Protestants and speaks about the chalice
sections.content_en:
Matijašević emphasizes the difference between humanitarian giving and giving for evangelization. **Everyone will give for a humanitarian purpose**, even an unbeliever when they see a great need. Only a believer will give for evangelization, because to an unbeliever it means nothing.

In this he also sees the reason why Protestants in the West are, as he says, more successful than Catholics. For Protestants, giving a tithe and investing in evangelization is a completely normal thing. Catholics, according to his words, would prefer everything to be a *„little stable”*, so they immediately wonder why everything in the church is so expensive.

The guest thinks differently: *„Well, let things be expensive.”* As an example, he takes the **chalice**. In it is the Blood of Christ which saved the believer, so let it even be made of diamonds, instead of an ordinary cup that some think is sufficient.

He also recounts an anecdote of a preacher who was furnishing a prayer hall. People offered him chairs that they no longer needed at home, and he responded with the question: *„Those chairs are not good enough for your house, but they are good enough for God's house?”* In the end, new chairs were placed in the hall. The reason, Matijašević says, is that **God deserves the best** and that such an attitude shows how much a person cares.

At the end of the chapter, he refers to the prophet **Haggai**. The people built their houses, and forgot God's house. That is why *„they pour into a purse, and it spills out for them”* and they sow, but do not reap. Blessing in one's own purses comes when one begins to build God's house.

sections.subtitle: Organizator koji plaća vlastitu kotizaciju: „Stavi novac tamo gdje su ti usta”
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o tome kako je i sam plaćao kotizaciju za Eho konferenciju
sections.content:
Matijašević svoje stavove potkrepljuje osobnim primjerom. **Prvih nekoliko godina Eho konferencije**, koju je sam organizirao, plaćao je kotizaciju kao i svaki drugi polaznik.

Objašnjava da je bio stava kako od drugih ne može tražiti da plate ako to sam nije spreman učiniti: *„Ja sam prvi u tome, ja prvi želim biti, meni je stalo. Ne mogu očekivati od nekoga da uloži u nešto gdje ja nisam spreman isto uložiti.”* Načelo sažima poznatom izrekom: *stavi novac tamo gdje su ti usta*.

Gost zatim prepričava rečenicu jednog propovjednika koja mu se posebno svidjela. Propovjednik je, nakon što je sa slušateljima podijelio sve što je imao, rekao: *„Ako sad ne date, vi ste mene pokrali. Jer vi ste od mene primili, a niste ništa vratili.”*

magisterium.assessment: Opis osobnog primjera organizatora koji sam plaća kotizaciju uglavnom je usklađen s kršćanskim načelom da vodstvo u Crkvi uključuje služenje i svjedočenje vlastitim životom. Odlomak iznosi praktično načelo dosljednosti, a ne tvrdnju da je plaćanje kotizacije vjerska obveza ili mjerilo nečije vjere.
magisterium.enrichment: Takav primjer podsjeća na Pavlov način rada: premda je imao pravo na potporu, trudio se ne biti drugima na teret i time im dati uzor, te je pozivao vjernike da ga nasljeduju kao što on nasljeduje Krista. Kristovo mjerilo vodstva ipak nije samo osobno ulaganje nego služenje drugima; zato kotizacija ne bi smjela postati znak nečije duhovne vrijednosti niti prepreka sudjelovanju siromašnijih.
magisterium.assessment_en: The description of the personal example of an organizer who pays the registration fee himself is largely aligned with the Christian principle that leadership in the Church includes serving and witnessing with one's own life. The passage presents a practical principle of consistency, not a claim that paying a registration fee is a religious obligation or a measure of someone's faith.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Such an example recalls Paul's way of working: although he had the right to support, he strived not to be a burden to others and thereby give them an example, and he called the faithful to imitate him as he imitates Christ. Christ's measure of leadership, however, is not only personal investment but serving others; therefore, a registration fee should not become a sign of someone's spiritual worth nor an obstacle to the participation of the poorer.

sections.subtitle_en: An organizer who pays his own registration fee: "Put your money where your mouth is"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about how he himself paid the registration fee for the Eho konferencija
sections.content_en:
Matijašević supports his stances with a personal example. **For the first several years of the Eho konferencija**, which he himself organized, he paid the registration fee just like any other attendee.

He explains that he held the stance that he could not ask others to pay if he was not ready to do so himself: *“I am first in that, I want to be first, I care. I cannot expect someone to invest in something where I am not ready to invest as well.”* He summarizes the principle with the well-known saying: *put your money where your mouth is*.

The guest then recounts a sentence of a preacher that he particularly liked. The preacher, after sharing with the listeners everything he had, said: *“If you do not give now, you have robbed me. Because you received from me, and you gave nothing back.”*

sections.subtitle: Korinćani ili Filipljani: Pavao i podrška onima koji služe Riječju
sections.screenshot_description: Matijašević uspoređuje Pavlov odnos prema Korinćanima i Filipljanima
sections.content:
Matijašević se osvrće na argument koji se, kako kaže, često koristi protiv plaćanja onih koji služe u Crkvi. Pavao je u Korintu sam izrađivao šatore i od Korinćana nije htio ništa uzeti. Gost odgovara protupitanjem: *„Jeste li sigurni da želite biti kao Korinćani?”*

Korinćane opisuje kao **nezrelu zajednicu**. Svađali su se oko toga tko je veći, na sastancima su se opijali i bludničili, a mučile su ih usporedbe i alkoholizam. Drugu poslanicu Korinćanima tumači kao Pavlov odgovor na prigovor da je u pismima prestrog, a uživo nije takav. Upravo zbog njihove nezrelosti Pavao im poručuje: *„Ove slave mi nećete oduzeti”*, i dolazi o vlastitom trošku.

S **Filipljanima** je bilo drukčije. Od njih je Pavao više puta primio pomoć. Njima je upućena molitva koju vjernici danas rado mole za financijski blagoslov: *„Bog moj pobrinut će se za svaku vašu potrebu raskošno prema bogatstvu svoje slave.”* Gost upozorava na kontekst: nekoliko redaka ranije Pavao zahvaljuje Filipljanima za podršku. Blagoslov je dakle molio za one koji su ga podržavali, a Korinćanima to nije rekao.

Matijašević navodi još dva mjesta:

- Pavlovo pitanje Korinćanima: ako je on njima sijao duhovna dobra, je li velika stvar ako od njih ubire materijalna?
- **Poslanicu Galaćanima**, za koju kaže da je ljudi zaboravljaju: onaj koji se poučava u Riječi neka dijeli svoja dobra s onim koji ga poučava.

*„Gdje je to danas?”*, pita se gost.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom točan kada kaže da se Pavao u Korintu uzdržavao vlastitim radom, ali njegova odluka nije dokaz da je primanje potpore znak nezrelosti: Pavao je smatrao da navjestitelji imaju pravo na uzdržavanje, a sam se toga prava odrekao radi posebnih pastoralnih razloga. Stoga je retoričko poistovjećivanje odbijanja potpore s nezrelošću Korinćana teološki nedovoljno utemeljeno.
concerns: Može se steći dojam da je Pavlovo samouzdržavanje bilo osuda svakog financijskog uzdržavanja crkvenih službenika, premda je Pavao izričito branio njihovo pravo da žive od naviještanja Evanđelja.

Opis Korinćana kao nezrelih može imati biblijsku osnovu, ali sam odlomak ne pokazuje kako se pojedini prijekori odnose na Pavlovu odluku da ne prima potporu. Izraz „alkoholizam” također bi trebalo rabiti oprezno: navod o opijanju ne utvrđuje sam po sebi ovisnost kao trajno stanje.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavlova praksa i njegovo načelno učenje treba razlikovati: imao je pravo na potporu, ali je u Korintu radio vlastitim rukama kako bi istaknuo besplatnost svoje službe i ne bi bio na teret zajednici. Zato njegova odluka nije opće pravilo da službenici Crkve ne smiju primati uzdržavanje; prema Pavlovu argumentu, vjernici mogu dijeliti materijalna dobra s onima koji im služe duhovnim dobrima.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is largely accurate when it says that Paul supported himself in Corinth through his own labor, but his decision is not proof that receiving support is a sign of immaturity: Paul considered that proclaimers have a right to maintenance, and he himself renounced that right for specific pastoral reasons. Therefore, rhetorically equating the refusal of support with the immaturity of the Corinthians is insufficiently grounded theologically.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul's practice and his principle teaching should be distinguished: he had a right to support, but in Corinth he worked with his own hands in order to emphasize the gratuitousness of his ministry and not be a burden to the community. Therefore, his decision is not a general rule that ministers of the Church may not receive maintenance; according to Paul's argument, believers may share material goods with those who serve them with spiritual goods.
concerns_en: The impression might be given that Paul's self-support was a condemnation of any financial support of church ministers, even though Paul explicitly defended their right to live by proclaiming the Gospel.

Describing the Corinthians as immature may have a biblical basis, but the passage itself does not show how individual reproofs relate to Paul's decision not to receive support. The term "alcoholism" should also be used with caution: the mention of drunkenness does not in itself establish addiction as a permanent condition.

sections.subtitle_en: Corinthians or Philippians: Paul and Support for Those Who Serve the Word
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matijašević compares Paul's relationship toward the Corinthians and Philippians
sections.content_en:
Matijašević reflects on the argument that, as he says, is often used against paying those who serve in the Church. In Corinth, Paul made tents himself and did not want to take anything from the Corinthians. The guest responds with a counter-question: *"Are you sure you want to be like the Corinthians?"*

He describes the Corinthians as an **immature community**. They argued over who was greater, at meetings they got drunk and committed fornication, and they were troubled by comparisons and alcoholism. He interprets the Second Epistle to the Corinthians as Paul's response to the objection that he is too strict in letters, but is not like that in person. Precisely because of their immaturity, Paul tells them: *"No one will rob me of this boast"*, and comes at his own expense.

With the **Philippians**, it was different. From them, Paul received help multiple times. To them is directed the prayer that believers today gladly pray for financial blessing: *"My God will supply every need of yours richly according to the riches of his glory."* The guest warns of the context: a few verses earlier Paul thanks the Philippians for their support. Thus, he prayed the blessing for those who supported him, and he did not say that to the Corinthians.

Matijašević cites two more passages:

- Paul's question to the Corinthians: if he sowed spiritual goods among them, is it a great thing if he reaps material goods from them?
- The **Epistle to the Galatians**, which he says people forget: let the one who is taught in the Word share his goods with the one who teaches him.

*"Where is that today?"*, the guest wonders.

sections.subtitle: Isusova kesa, nardova pomast i konferencija od 25.000 eura
sections.screenshot_description: Gost govori o troškovima organizacije današnjih evangelizacijskih događaja
sections.content:
Matijašević odbacuje i tvrdnju da Isus ništa nije uzimao. Isus i učenici imali su zajedničku kesu, pa se gost pita od čega su živjeli: *„Nisu svaki put izvadili novac iz ribljih usta.”* Postojala je, dakle, neka podrška. Isus doduše nije nakon okupljanja skupljao milodar, ali nije ni imao iste uvjete kao današnji organizatori.

Te uvjete gost opisuje konkretnim brojkama. Organizacija konferencije može stajati, primjerice, **25.000 eura**. Netko će se ipak buniti: *„25 eura za slavljenje Boga?”* Matijašević odgovara da Boga svatko može slaviti kod kuće, besplatno, ali organizacija ima svoju cijenu. Vlasnik dvorane od 8.000 eura neće je ustupiti besplatno samo zato što će se u njoj slaviti Boga.

Takve izgovore uspoređuje s **Judom**, koji je prigovorio ženi što je prolila skupocjenu nardovu pomast umjesto da je proda i novac podijeli siromasima. Isus je odgovorio: *„Siromahe ćete uvijek imati.”* Gost napominje da je ta pomast vrijedila koliko jednogodišnja plaća.

Isto vrijedi i za apostole. Istina je da sami nisu imali ništa, ali ljudi su prodavali imanja i polagali im novac pred noge, a tim se novcem gradila Crkva. Današnji vjernici, zaključuje Matijašević, žele da im vjera rješava probleme, ali nisu spremni to isto podržati.

magisterium.assessment: Tvrdnja da su Isus i apostoli imali zajedničku kesu te da evangelizacija i crkvene aktivnosti mogu zahtijevati materijalnu potporu načelno je u skladu s kršćanskom praksom i naukom. Ipak, iznos od 25.000 eura i odgovor na prigovor o cijeni nisu dovoljni da bi se procijenilo jesu li troškovi razmjerni, transparentni i predstavljeni bez pritiska na vjernike.
concerns: Nije navedeno što sve ulazi u trošak konferencije ni zašto je baš taj iznos potreban; sam iznos ne dokazuje ni opravdanost ni neprimjerenost trošenja.

Ako se naplata predstavlja kao cijena za slavljenje Boga ili kao uvjet za sudjelovanje u sakramentalnom životu, to bi bilo problematično: crkveno služenje ne smije ostavljati dojam da je podložno tarifi.
Odlomak je prekinut usred odgovora („da Boga…”), pa se ne može pouzdano procijeniti puni argument ni način na koji se govori o nardovoj pomasti i siromasima.
magisterium.enrichment: Evanđelja spominju zajedničku kesu Isusa i učenika, a crkvene ustanove i evangelizacijski pothvati opravdano imaju stvarne troškove; potpora tim potrebama može biti izraz suodgovornosti i solidarnosti. No, Isusova pohvala pomazanju ne treba se koristiti za zanemarivanje siromaha: crkveni tekst o tom događaju povezuje Isusovo tumačenje pomasti s neraskidivom povezanošću evanđeoskog navještaja i brige za siromašne. Zato je važno razlikovati dobrovoljni doprinos za troškove od naplaćivanja sakramenata ili stvaranja dojma da se Božje milosti kupuju.
magisterium.assessment_en: The claim that Jesus and the apostles had a common purse and that evangelization and ecclesial activities may require material support is in principle aligned with Christian practice and teaching. Nevertheless, the amount of 25,000 euros and the response to the objection about the price are not sufficient to assess whether the costs are proportionate, transparent, and presented without pressure on the faithful.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Gospels mention the common purse of Jesus and the disciples, and ecclesial institutions and evangelization endeavors legitimately incur real costs; supporting these needs can be an expression of co-responsibility and solidarity. However, Jesus' praise of the anointing should not be used to neglect the poor: church teaching on that event links Jesus' interpretation of the ointment with the indissoluble connection between the proclamation of the Gospel and care for the poor. Therefore, it is important to distinguish a voluntary contribution toward costs from charging for sacraments or creating the impression that God's graces are being bought.
concerns_en: It is not specified what is included in the conference cost nor why that specific amount is needed; the amount itself proves neither the justification nor the impropriety of the expenditure.

If charging is presented as a price for praising God or as a condition for participating in sacramental life, that would be problematic: ecclesial ministry must not leave the impression of being subject to a fee schedule.
The excerpt is interrupted in the middle of the response ("that God..."), so the full argument and the manner in which the nard ointment and the poor are discussed cannot be reliably assessed.

sections.subtitle_en: Jesus' purse, nard ointment, and a 25,000-euro conference
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest speaks about the costs of organizing today's evangelization events
sections.content_en:
Matijašević also rejects the claim that Jesus took nothing. Jesus and the disciples had a common purse, so the guest asks what they lived on: *„They did not pull money out of a fish's mouth every time.”* There was, therefore, some support. Jesus, to be sure, did not collect an offering after gatherings, but neither did He have the same conditions as today's organizers.

The guest describes those conditions with concrete numbers. Organizing a conference can cost, for example, **25,000 euros**. Someone will still protest: *„25 euros for praising God?”* Matijašević replies that anyone can praise God at home, for free, but organization has its price. The owner of an 8,000-euro hall will not grant it for free just because God will be praised in it.

He compares such excuses to **Judas**, who objected to the woman pouring out expensive nard ointment instead of selling it and distributing the money to the poor. Jesus replied: *„The poor you will always have.”* The guest notes that this ointment was worth as much as a one-year salary.

The same applies to the apostles. The truth is that they themselves had nothing, but people sold properties and laid the money at their feet, and with that money the Church was built. Today's believers, Matijašević concludes, want faith to solve their problems, but they are not ready to support that very thing.

sections.subtitle: Milost je besplatna, ali nije bezvrijedna: koljeno od pola milijuna i operacija od 5.000 eura
sections.screenshot_description: Matijašević prepričava primjer ozdravljenja nakon molitve
sections.content:
Na prigovor da se ne može naplaćivati nešto što je primljeno besplatno, Matijašević odgovara jasnim razlikovanjem. **Milost se ne može naplatiti, ali vrijeme može.** Mogao je biti negdje drugdje i zarađivati novac, a svoje je vrijeme posvetio ovoj službi. Onima koji ga podsjećaju da je i sam besplatno primio, s dozom ironije poručuje neka i oni odu i besplatno prime, pa neka rade isto što i on.

Poantu da besplatno ne znači bezvrijedno ilustrira s dva primjera:

- **Rukometaš Duvnjak** imao je, kako kaže, koljeno osigurano na pola milijuna eura. Gost se u šali pita: kad bi zajednica molila za njegovo bolesno koljeno i ono ozdravilo, bi li uplatio donaciju od pola milijuna? Sumnja u to, jer bi se tada i 500 eura činilo mnogo.
- **Stvarni slučaj s molitvenog susreta**: ženi s problemom diska u leđima nakon molitve se vratila mogućnost pokreta koji prije nije mogla izvesti. Mjesec dana kasnije stanje je i dalje bilo dobro. U isto vrijeme sestra jedne gostu poznate osobe, zbog neizdržive boli, platila je privatnu operaciju istog problema **5.000 eura**.

Matijašević se pita bi li donacija nakon takvog ozdravljenja bila blizu 5.000 eura koji bi ostali u džepu. Zaključuje da ne bi, i da bi se i 100 eura smatralo velikim darom, iako su ljudi spremni platiti mnogo da bi dobili zdravlje. Ono što je besplatno, ponavlja, ne znači da ništa ne vrijedi niti da se trud ne smije nagraditi, kako bi ljudi i dalje ustrajali u službi.

magisterium.assessment: Razlikovanje između besplatnosti milosti i stvarne vrijednosti ljudskog rada može biti u skladu s katoličkim naukom: služitelj može primati potporu za svoj rad, ali Evanđelje i sakramentalni život ne smiju se pretvoriti u robu. Odlomak ipak ne objašnjava dovoljno što se konkretno naplaćuje, pa iz njega nije moguće procijeniti je li riječ o primjerenoj potpori ili komercijalizaciji služenja.
concerns: Izjava „vrijeme može [se naplatiti]” može biti opravdana ako se odnosi na poštenu naknadu za rad, ali postaje problematična ako se njome cijena veže uz primanje milosti, molitve, ozdravljenja ili sakramenata; odlomak tu granicu ne razjašnjava.
Ironičan odgovor kritičarima ne pobija njihovu moguću teološku primjedbu i može skrenuti pozornost s potrebne jasnoće o tome kako se sredstva prikupljaju i za što se koriste.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusove riječi „Besplatno ste primili, besplatno dajte” pozivaju na velikodušnost u naviještanju i služenju, a ne znače da rad služitelja nema stvarnu vrijednost. Crkva istodobno upozorava da se sakramentalni život ne komercijalizira te da darovi vjernika moraju ostati slobodni prilozi, a ne cijena ili obvezna naknada; zato je važno jasno razlikovati potporu služitelju od naplaćivanja Božje milosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The distinction between the gratuitousness of grace and the real value of human labor can be in accordance with Catholic teaching: a minister may receive support for his work, but the Gospel and sacramental life must not be turned into a commodity. The passage, however, does not explain sufficiently what specifically is being charged for, so from it, it is not possible to assess whether this is appropriate support or the commercialization of ministry.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus's words "Freely you have received, freely give" call for generosity in proclamation and ministry, and do not mean that a minister's work has no real value. At the same time, the Church warns that sacramental life must not be commercialized and that gifts of the faithful must remain free offerings, not a price or mandatory fee; that is why it is important to clearly distinguish support for a minister from charging for God's grace.
concerns_en: The statement "time can [be charged for]" can be justified if it refers to fair compensation for labor, but it becomes problematic if it attaches a price to receiving grace, prayer, healings, or sacraments; the passage does not clarify this boundary.
The ironic response to critics does not refute their possible theological objection and may deflect attention from the necessary clarity about how funds are collected and what they are used for.

sections.subtitle_en: Grace is free, but not worthless: a half-million knee and a 5,000-euro surgery
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matijašević recounts an example of healing after prayer
sections.content_en:
To the objection that one cannot charge for something received freely, Matijašević responds with a clear distinction. **Grace cannot be charged for, but time can.** He could have been elsewhere earning money, but he dedicated his time to this ministry. To those who remind him that he himself received freely, with a touch of irony he tells them to go and receive freely as well, and then do the same as he does.

He illustrates the point that free does not mean worthless with two examples:

- **Handball player Duvnjak** had, as he says, his knee insured for half a million euros. The guest jokingly asks: if the community prayed for his diseased knee and it healed, would he pay a donation of half a million? He doubts it, because then even 500 euros would seem like a lot.
- **A real case from a prayer meeting**: for a woman with a spinal disc problem, after prayer the ability to make a movement she previously could not perform returned. A month later, the condition was still good. At the same time, the sister of a person known to the guest, due to unbearable pain, paid **5,000 euros** for private surgery for the same problem.

Matijašević wonders whether a donation after such a healing would be anywhere near the 5,000 euros that remained in the pocket. He concludes that it would not, and that even 100 euros would be considered a great gift, even though people are ready to pay a lot to obtain health. What is free, he repeats, does not mean that it is worth nothing nor that effort must not be rewarded, so that people may continue to persevere in ministry.

sections.subtitle: Novac kao test vjernosti: 20 kuna u crkvi, 100 kuna za rundu
sections.screenshot_description: Gost uspoređuje davanje u crkvi s plaćanjem računa u birtiji
sections.content:
Matijašević zaključuje da je **novac test naše vjernosti**. Odnos prema novcu i ono na što ga trošimo pokazuje što nam je važno i koliko zapravo vjerujemo Bogu.

Krunoslav se nadovezuje mišlju: *„Svemu znamo cijenu, ali ničemu ne znamo pravu vrijednost.”* Opisuje iskustvo s vlastitih konferencija. Ljudi se žale na cijenu, iako su postojale vrlo rane i rane prijave po nižim cijenama. Na pitanje gdje su bili pola godine ranije, odgovaraju da nisu znali, iako su događaj mogli pratiti. Mogućnosti se uvijek nude, kaže voditelj, a o vjernicima ovisi hoće li ih prihvatiti. Upravo to pokazuje koliko im je do nečega stalo.

Gost u tome vidi poznat obrazac: **novac u Crkvi uvijek ima puno veću težinu nego u birtiji**. Prisjeća se vremena kuna. Za 10 ili 20 kuna u crkvi ljudi će se pobrinuti da se vidi, pa će čak i dijete poslati da ubaci novac pred svima. Sto kuna za rundu u kafiću nije nikakav problem, a 20 kuna u crkvi smatra se velikim darom.

Davanje Bogu, objašnjava Matijašević, nije izraz njegove potrebe, nego **zahvalnosti**. Kod Židova je taj novac išao onima koji su Bogu služili, kako bi mogli nastaviti služiti, a darivatelj je time pokazivao zahvalnost za ono što je primio.

magisterium.assessment: Tvrdnja da odnos prema novcu može razotkriti naše prioritete i vjernost Bogu uglavnom je u skladu s Isusovim upozorenjem da se ne može služiti i Bogu i bogatstvu te s kršćanskim pozivom da se imovina koristi odgovorno i velikodušno. Ipak, novčani izbori sami po sebi ne omogućuju pouzdano prosuđivanje nečije vjere, osobito bez uvida u njegove okolnosti i obveze.
concerns: Izraz da novac pokazuje „koliko zapravo vjerujemo Bogu” može zvučati kao pojednostavljeno mjerilo vjere ili poticati procjenjivanje drugih prema njihovoj potrošnji; kršćansko učenje upozorava na navezanost na bogatstvo, ali ne osuđuje samo posjedovanje novca.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćansko pitanje nije samo koliko netko daje ili troši, nego služi li novac Bogu i bližnjemu ili postaje idol koji zatvara srce. Crkveno učenje naglašava da su dobra, i kad su zakonito stečena, namijenjena i zajedničkom dobru, a vjernici su njihovi upravitelji; stoga je velikodušnost važna, ali se prosuđuje uz razboritost i stvarne životne okolnosti.
