magisterium.assessment_en: The claim that the attitude toward money can reveal our priorities and faithfulness to God is largely in accordance with Jesus's warning that one cannot serve both God and wealth, and with the Christian call to use property responsibly and generously. However, monetary choices by themselves do not allow for a reliable judgment of someone's faith, especially without insight into their circumstances and obligations.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Christian question is not only how much someone gives or spends, but whether money serves God and neighbor or becomes an idol that closes the heart. Church teaching emphasizes that goods, even when lawfully acquired, are also destined for the common good, and the faithful are their stewards; therefore, generosity is important, but it is judged alongside prudence and actual life circumstances.
concerns_en: The expression that money shows “how much we actually trust God” can sound like a simplified measure of faith or encourage evaluating others based on their spending; Christian teaching warns against attachment to wealth, but does not condemn the mere possession of money.

sections.subtitle_en: Money as a test of faithfulness: 20 kuna in church, 100 kuna for a round of drinks
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest compares giving in church with paying the bill in a bar
sections.content_en:
Matijašević concludes that **money is a test of our faithfulness**. The attitude toward money and what we spend it on shows what is important to us and how much we actually trust God.

Krunoslav follows up with the thought: *“We know the price of everything, but we do not know the true value of anything.”* He describes the experience from his own conferences. People complain about the price, even though there were super early bird and early bird registrations at lower prices. When asked where they were half a year earlier, they answer that they did not know, even though they could have followed the event. Opportunities are always offered, says the host, and it depends on the faithful whether they will accept them. That is precisely what shows how much they care about something.

The guest sees a familiar pattern in this: **money in the Church always carries much more weight than in a bar**. He recalls the time of the kuna. For 10 or 20 kuna in church, people will make sure it is seen, so they will even send a child to drop the money in front of everyone. One hundred kuna for a round in a cafe is no problem at all, while 20 kuna in church is considered a great gift.

Giving to God, Matijašević explains, is not an expression of His need, but of **gratitude**. Among the Jews, that money went to those who served God, so that they could continue to serve, and by doing so, the giver showed gratitude for what he had received.

sections.subtitle: Ne vlasnici, nego upravitelji: nove felge i deset eura donacije
sections.screenshot_description: Matijašević objašnjava da čovjek nije vlasnik novca, nego upravitelj
sections.content:
Temu financija Matijašević zaokružuje načelom koje smatra temeljnim: **čovjek nije vlasnik novca, nego upravitelj**. Upravlja onim što mu je povjereno, a pravi Vlasnik jednoga će ga dana pitati što je s tim učinio.

Odgovor mnogih vjernika gost slikovito karikira: *„Kupio sam nove felge. A onda sam tamo donirao deset eura i bio sam dobar vjernik.”* Krunoslav dodaje s ironijom: *„Valjaš, slugo dobri i vjerni”*, i primjećuje da si tako sami tepamo.

Matijašević pojašnjava da nema ništa protiv novih felgi. Važno mu je da omjer između onoga što je netko spreman uložiti u Božje stvari i onoga što ulaže u propadljivo bude barem približan.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak da je čovjek pred Bogom upravitelj povjerenih dobara, odgovoran za njihovu uporabu i pozvan na velikodušnost, dobro je usklađen s katoličkim naukom i biblijskim motivom vjernog upravitelja. Treba ga razumjeti uz nauk da je privatno vlasništvo legitimno, ali da njegova uporaba nosi društvenu i moralnu odgovornost; odlomak ne daje dovoljno konteksta da bi se procijenile njegove daljnje tvrdnje nakon nedovršene rečenice „Važno…”.
concerns: Izraz „čovjek nije vlasnik novca” može biti neprecizan ako se shvati kao poricanje legitimnog privatnog vlasništva; katolički nauk razlikuje pravo posjedovanja od obveze da se dobra koriste odgovorno i uvažavaju potrebe drugih.

Ironično preoblikovanje Isusovih riječi „Valjaš, slugo dobri i vjerni” moglo bi zvučati neozbiljno ako bi se izdvojilo iz konteksta, ali u prikazanom odlomku služi kritici samodopadnog opravdavanja minimalne donacije.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkveni nauk ne traži da se odrekne svake osobne imovine: Rerum Novarum potvrđuje pravo privatnog vlasništva, ali uči da se dobra, nakon što se razumno podmire vlastite i obiteljske potrebe, trebaju dijeliti s potrebitima. Upravljanje dobrima zato uključuje i razboritost i velikodušnost, a ne samo određeni iznos ili postotak donacije; važno je da materijalna dobra služe Bogu i bližnjemu, a ne sebičnom gomilanju.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis that man is a steward of entrusted goods before God, responsible for their use and called to generosity, is well aligned with Catholic teaching and the biblical motif of the faithful steward. It should be understood alongside the teaching that private property is legitimate, but that its use carries social and moral responsibility; the passage does not provide enough context to assess his further claims following the unfinished sentence „Important…”.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Church teaching does not demand the renunciation of all personal property: Rerum Novarum confirms the right of private property, but teaches that goods, once one's own and family needs are reasonably met, should be shared with the needy. The stewardship of goods therefore includes both prudence and generosity, and not merely a certain amount or percentage of a donation; it is important that material goods serve God and neighbor, and not selfish accumulation.
concerns_en: The phrase „man is not the owner of money” can be imprecise if understood as a denial of legitimate private property; Catholic teaching distinguishes the right of ownership from the duty to use goods responsibly and take into account the needs of others.

The ironic rephrasing of Jesus's words „You're good, good and faithful servant” could sound flippant if taken out of context, but in the presented passage it serves as a critique of the smug justification of a minimal donation.

sections.subtitle_en: Not owners, but stewards: new rims and a ten-euro donation
sections.screenshot_description_en: Matijašević explains that man is not the owner of money, but a steward
sections.content_en:
Matijašević rounds off the topic of finances with a principle he considers fundamental: **man is not the owner of money, but a steward**. He manages what has been entrusted to him, and one day the true Owner will ask him what he did with it.

The guest vividly caricatures the response of many believers: *„I bought new rims. And then I donated ten euros there and I was a good believer.”* Krunoslav adds with irony: *„You're good, good and faithful servant”*, and observes that that is how we flatter ourselves.

Matijašević clarifies that he has nothing against new rims. It is important to him that the ratio between what someone is ready to invest in God's things and what they invest in the perishable is at least approximate.

sections.subtitle: Blic pitanja: pastir zbog utjecaja, služenje kao preduvjet vodstva
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj postavlja prvo blic pitanje „radnik ili pastir”
sections.content:
Primjećujući da je vrijeme proletjelo, Krunoslav najavljuje završni **„ili-ili” izazov**. Gost bira jednu od dviju ponuđenih opcija, koje su ponekad namjerno kontroverzne, a uvijek može ponuditi i treću i kratko je obrazložiti.

**Radnik ili pastir?** Na pitanje o radniku na Božjoj njivi ili pastiru Matijašević prvo priznaje da mu je jednostavnije biti radnik. Radnik odradi svoj dio, a odgovornost je na nekom drugom. Ipak bira **pastira**, jer pastir vodi, upravlja i ima priliku utjecati na one koje vodi, kao i na one koji će dalje utjecati na druge. Pastir ima veću odgovornost, ali i više prostora za utjecaj. Krunoslav to sažima: po pitanju utjecaja, pastir.

**Voditi ljude ili služiti ljudima?** Gost bira **služenje**. Smatra da se ne može voditi bez služenja, jer vođa mora biti dostupan, a vodstvo uključuje mnogo toga što je zapravo služenje. Krunoslav dodaje da je to Isus pokazao svojim primjerom.

magisterium.assessment: Izbor pastira koji vodi i preuzima odgovornost može biti u skladu s kršćanskim shvaćanjem vodstva, ali odlomak naglašava upravljanje i utjecaj, a ne izričito služenje, brigu za povjerene osobe ili odgovornost pred Bogom. Zato je izjava djelomično usklađena: njezino značenje ovisi o tome shvaća li se utjecaj kao sredstvo služenja ili kao cilj sam po sebi.
concerns: Naglašavanje mogućnosti utjecaja može ostaviti dojam da je pastirska uloga poželjna zbog moći ili osobnog utjecaja; Isus, naprotiv, razlikuje kršćansko vodstvo od gospodarenja nad drugima.
magisterium.enrichment: Isus u Mk 10,42–45 uči da onaj tko želi biti velik treba služiti, jer Sin Čovječji nije došao da bude služen, nego da služi i dade svoj život za mnoge. Stoga su vođenje i upravljanje u Crkvi vjerodostojni kada se vrše ponizno, radi dobra zajednice i kao odgovorna briga za povjereno stado, a ne radi vlastite važnosti ili samopotvrđivanja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The choice of a shepherd who leads and assumes responsibility can be in accordance with the Christian understanding of leadership, but the passage emphasizes management and influence, rather than explicitly service, care for the entrusted persons, or responsibility before God. Therefore, the statement is partially aligned: its meaning depends on whether influence is understood as a means of service or as an end in itself.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Mk 10:42–45, Jesus teaches that whoever wishes to be great must serve, for the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life for many. Therefore, leading and governance in the Church are authentic when exercised humbly, for the good of the community, and as responsible care for the entrusted flock, rather than for one's own importance or self-affirmation.
concerns_en: Emphasizing the possibility of influence can leave the impression that the pastoral role is desirable because of power or personal influence; Jesus, on the contrary, distinguishes Christian leadership from lording it over others.

sections.subtitle_en: Flash questions: shepherd because of influence, service as a prerequisite for leadership
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host asks the first flash question "worker or shepherd"
sections.content_en:
Noticing that time has flown by, Krunoslav announces the final **"either-or" challenge**. The guest chooses one of the two offered options, which are sometimes deliberately controversial, and can always offer a third one and briefly explain it.

**Worker or shepherd?** To the question about a worker in God's field or a shepherd, Matijašević first admits that it is simpler for him to be a worker. A worker does his part, and the responsibility lies with someone else. Still, he chooses **shepherd**, because a shepherd leads, manages, and has the opportunity to influence those he leads, as well as those who will further influence others. A shepherd has greater responsibility, but also more room for influence. Krunoslav summarizes it: in terms of influence, a shepherd.

**To lead people or to serve people?** The guest chooses **service**. He believes that one cannot lead without serving, because a leader must be accessible, and leadership includes much that is actually service. Krunoslav adds that Jesus showed this by his example.

sections.subtitle: Postojanost umjesto karizme i srce kralja Davida
sections.screenshot_description: Gost objašnjava zašto bira kralja Davida
sections.content:
**Karizma ili postojanost?** Iako dolazi iz karizmatskog pokreta i karizmatske zajednice, Matijašević bez dvojbe bira **postojanost**. Smatra da upravo ona danas nedostaje: *„Život nije samo jedna dobra duhovna obnova, život je goriti i ostati gorjeti do kraja.”*

**Kraljevstvo Božje ili kraljevstvo ovoga svijeta?** To pitanje Krunoslav sam naziva lakšim, a gost kratko odgovara: **Kraljevstvo Božje**.

**Sveti Josip ili kralj David?** Ovo je, kako je voditelj najavio, najteže pitanje. Nakon kraće stanke gost napominje da o svetom Josipu nema mnogo zapisa i bira **kralja Davida**: *„David je bio lik.”* Krunoslav dodaje da se David znao dobro pokajati. Matijašević se slaže, ali ističe nešto drugo: Davidu je srce baš gorjelo. Ne tvrdi da Josipu nije, ali među biblijskim likovima David se posebno ističe. Započeo je viziju gradnje doma Jahvina i bilo mu je stalo do toga. Unatoč trenucima slabosti i grijeha, iz njegovih se psalama vidi srce usmjereno prema Gospodinu.

Odgovor završava osobnom željom. Gledajući svoj život, Matijašević bi volio da i njegovo srce, unatoč svemu, gori za Božjom prisutnošću i njegovim domom.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na postojanosti, Kraljevstvu Božjem i Davidu kao biblijskoj osobi uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim naukom; postojanost do kraja odražava kršćanski poziv na vjernost, a Božje je Kraljevstvo vječno i nadilazi zemaljska kraljevstva. Iz odlomka se ne vidi ništa što bi izravno proturječilo Svetom pismu ili nauku Crkve.
concerns: Izraz „goriti i ostati gorjeti do kraja” prikladna je slika za ustrajnost, ali ne bi ga trebalo razumjeti kao da se vjernost oslanja samo na ljudsku snagu ili trajni osjećaj duhovnog žara: kršćanska se postojanost živi uz Božju milost.
Napomena da o svetom Josipu nema mnogo zapisa u Svetom pismu općenito je točna, no kratki ulomak ne daje dovoljno konteksta da bi se procijenilo kako gost dalje uspoređuje Josipa i Davida.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička duhovna tradicija povezuje ustrajnost s Božjom pomoći: vjernik je pozvan biti vjeran do kraja, ali ustrajnost je i dar za koji se moli, a ne tek rezultat vlastitog napora. Biblijska obećanja Davidu usmjerena su prema trajnom kraljevstvu koje se u kršćanskom čitanju ispunja u Kristu; zato izbor Kraljevstva Božjeg ne znači prezir prema svakodnevnim obvezama, nego davanje prvenstva Božjoj vladavini i njezinim vrijednostima.

citations.document_title: On the Love of God - Book III

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on steadfastness, the Kingdom of God, and David as a biblical figure is generally in accordance with Catholic teaching; steadfastness to the end reflects the Christian call to faithfulness, and the Kingdom of God is eternal and transcends earthly kingdoms. Nothing is seen from the excerpt that would directly contradict Sacred Scripture or the teaching of the Church.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic spiritual tradition links perseverance with God's help: the believer is called to be faithful to the end, but perseverance is also a gift prayed for, and not merely the result of one's own effort. Biblical promises to David are directed toward an enduring kingdom that in Christian reading is fulfilled in Christ; therefore, choosing the Kingdom of God does not mean contempt for everyday obligations, but giving priority to God's reign and its values.
concerns_en: The expression „to burn and remain burning until the end” is a fitting image for perseverance, but it should not be understood as if faithfulness relies only on human strength or an enduring feeling of spiritual fervor: Christian steadfastness is lived with God's grace.

The note that there are not many records about Saint Joseph in Sacred Scripture is generally accurate, but the short excerpt does not provide enough context to assess how the guest further compares Joseph and David.

sections.subtitle_en: Steadfastness instead of charisma and the heart of King David
sections.screenshot_description_en: The guest explains why he chooses King David
sections.content_en:
**Charisma or steadfastness?** Even though he comes from the charismatic movement and a charismatic community, Matijašević without a doubt chooses **steadfastness**. He considers that this is precisely what is lacking today: *„Life is not just one good spiritual renewal, life is to burn and remain burning until the end.”*

**The Kingdom of God or the kingdom of this world?** Krunoslav himself calls this question easier, and the guest briefly answers: **The Kingdom of God**.

**Saint Joseph or King David?** This is, as the host announced, the most difficult question. After a brief pause, the guest notes that there are not many records about Saint Joseph and chooses **King David**: *„David was a character.”* Krunoslav adds that David knew how to repent well. Matijašević agrees, but emphasizes something else: David's heart truly burned. He does not claim that Joseph's did not, but among biblical figures David stands out in particular. He began the vision of building the house of Yahweh and cared about it. Despite moments of weakness and sin, his psalms show a heart directed toward the Lord.

The answer ends with a personal wish. Looking at his life, Matijašević would like his heart also, despite everything, to burn for God's presence and His house.

sections.subtitle: Izazov za idući mjesec: zapisujte svaki pad u obrazac koji želite promijeniti
sections.screenshot_description: Marko Matijašević zadaje gledateljima izazov za sljedeći mjesec
sections.content:
Na kraju razgovora Krunoslav moli gosta da gledateljima zada izazov za idući mjesec. To može biti nešto korisno za partnerske odnose, obitelj ili posao, nešto što mu je trenutno na srcu.

Matijašević, koji je izazov u šali nazvao „zadaćom”, predlaže praktičnu vježbu u dva koraka:

- **Odaberite jedan obrazac ponašanja** koji želite mijenjati.
- **Svaki dan zapisujte** kad ste upali u taj obrazac.

Tek nakon toga treba tražiti **protuobrazac**, odnosno ponašanje prema kojem se želi ići. Prvi mjesec služi tome da se osvijesti svaki trenutak kad se čovjek nađe u starom obrascu, jer, kako kaže, *„dok ne skužimo što radimo, ne možemo ni ispravljati”*.

Vježba se može primijeniti na partnerski odnos, financije, posao ili odnose sa zaposlenicima i kolegama. Područje je nebitno, važno je pronaći ono što se želi promijeniti i bilježiti koliko često se u to pada. Izazov se nadovezuje na misao koju je gost iznio ranije u epizodi: djeca i drugi oko nas upijaju ono što mi jesmo, pa je rad na vlastitim obrascima stalna zadaća.

magisterium.assessment: Predloženo svakodnevno bilježenje obrasca ponašanja i promišljanje o željenoj promjeni uglavnom je u skladu s katoličkim razumijevanjem moralnog rasta i preobrazbe života. Sveto pismo govori o odlaganju staroga čovjeka i obnovi duha uma, ali iz odlomka nije jasno povezuje li se vježba i s Božjom milošću te rastom u kreposti.
concerns: Vježba može ostati na razini samopromatranja i samodiscipline ako se ne nadopuni molitvom, pouzdanjem u Božju milost i konkretnim kreposnim djelovanjem; odlomak ne tvrdi da je to dovoljno, ali to ne spominje.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolička moralna tradicija prepoznaje važnost ponavljanih čina u oblikovanju navika i kreposti, pa opažanje ponavljajućeg obrasca može pomoći u razlučivanju što treba mijenjati. Ipak, kršćanska promjena nije samo zamjena jedne navike drugom: ona uključuje suradnju s milošću, usmjerenost prema dobru i njegovanje odnosa s Bogom.
magisterium.assessment_en: The proposed daily recording of a behavioral pattern and reflection on the desired change is generally in accordance with the Catholic understanding of moral growth and the transformation of life. Sacred Scripture speaks of putting off the old self and the renewal of the spirit of the mind, but from the passage it is not clear whether the exercise is also connected with God's grace and growth in virtue.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic moral tradition recognizes the importance of repeated acts in the formation of habits and virtues, so observing a repeating pattern can help in discerning what needs to be changed. Still, Christian change is not merely replacing one habit with another: it involves cooperation with grace, orientation toward the good, and nurturing a relationship with God.
concerns_en: The exercise may remain at the level of self-observation and self-discipline if it is not supplemented by prayer, trust in God's grace, and concrete virtuous action; the passage does not claim that this is sufficient, but it does not mention it.

sections.subtitle_en: Challenge for the next month: write down every fall into the pattern you want to change
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marko Matijašević gives viewers a challenge for the next month
sections.content_en:
At the end of the conversation, Krunoslav asks the guest to give the viewers a challenge for the next month. It can be something useful for partner relationships, family, or work, something currently on his heart.

Matijašević, who jokingly called the challenge "homework", proposes a practical two-step exercise:

- **Choose one pattern of behavior** that you want to change.
- **Write down every day** when you have fallen into that pattern.

Only after that should one look for a **counter-pattern**, that is, the behavior toward which one wants to go. The first month serves to become aware of every moment when a person finds themselves in the old pattern, because, as he says, *"until we figure out what we are doing, we cannot even correct it"*.

The exercise can be applied to a partner relationship, finances, work, or relationships with employees and colleagues. The area is irrelevant; what matters is finding what one wants to change and recording how often one falls into it. The challenge builds on a thought the guest expressed earlier in the episode: children and others around us absorb what we are, so working on our own patterns is an ongoing task.

sections.subtitle: Cvijeće za godišnjicu, odjava i najava: sjećanje na oslobađanje Banovine
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj zahvaljuje gostu i šali se na račun godišnjice braka
sections.content:
Krunoslav zahvaljuje gostu na izdvojenom vremenu i šali se na račun činjenice, spomenute ranije u razgovoru, da Matijašević na dan **osme godišnjice braka** s Mirjanom gostuje u podcastu. Savjetuje mu da nakon snimanja otrči u cvjećarnu, ako još radi, i kupi cvijeće, kako kod kuće ne bi bilo problema. Gost uzvraća da danas to neće biti problem i zahvaljuje na pozivu.

Voditelj zatim zahvaljuje gledateljima što prate podcast **Redefinicija** i poziva ih da postanu članovi na **Patreonu**, gdje sljedeću epizodu mogu pogledati već danas. Emisija se zatvara pozdravom: *„Vidimo se u Redefiniciji.”*

Slijedi isječak iz sljedeće epizode. Sugovornik prepričava ratno sjećanje: izišao je van i pitao sprema li se nešto i kreće li se u oslobađanje. Kad je dobio potvrdan odgovor i savjet da se makne, u auto je stavio knjige, **župne matice** i ono što je imao te krenuo *„kao neki slalom između tenkova”* prema Zagrebu. Na putu od Siska prema selima čuo je početak kanonade. Bilo je to oko pet sati ujutro, kada je hrvatsko topništvo započelo pripremu za **oslobađanje Banovine**.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ne iznosi značajnije teološke tvrdnje, pa se ne može prosuđivati kao poučavanje katoličkog nauka; zahvala, čestitka za godišnjicu braka i poziv na Patreon sami po sebi nisu u neskladu s njim. U prikazanom sadržaju nema očitog proturječja Svetom pismu ili katoličkom nauku.
magisterium.enrichment: U katoličkom razumijevanju, brak nije samo povod za osobnu čestitku: ženidbeni sakrament poziva supružnike da svojim životom svjedoče ljubav koja povezuje Krista i Crkvu. Ivan Pavao II. opisuje supružnike kao posvećene Bogu za sveto služenje i trajno svjedočenje te ljubavi.
magisterium.assessment_en: The passage does not make significant theological assertions, so it cannot be judged as teaching Catholic doctrine; thanks, congratulations on a wedding anniversary, and an invitation to Patreon in themselves are not in discord with it. In the presented content there is no obvious contradiction to Sacred Scripture or Catholic teaching.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Catholic understanding, marriage is not merely an occasion for personal congratulations: the sacrament of marriage calls spouses to witness with their lives to the love that unites Christ and the Church. John Paul II describes spouses as consecrated to God for holy service and the permanent witnessing of that love.

sections.subtitle_en: Flowers for an anniversary, sign-off, and announcement: memory of the liberation of Banovina
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host thanks the guest and jokes about the wedding anniversary
sections.content_en:
Krunoslav thanks the guest for his time and jokes about the fact, mentioned earlier in the conversation, that Matijašević is guesting on the podcast on the day of his **eighth wedding anniversary** with Mirjana. He advises him to run to a flower shop after the recording, if it is still open, and buy flowers so there would be no problems at home. The guest replies that today that will not be a problem and thanks him for the invitation.

The host then thanks the viewers for following the podcast **Redefinicija** and invites them to become members on **Patreon**, where they can watch the next episode as early as today. The show closes with the greeting: *„See you in Redefinicija.”*

A clip from the next episode follows. The interlocutor recounts a wartime memory: he went outside and asked if something was brewing and if a move toward liberation was starting. When he received an affirmative answer and advice to get away, he put books, **parish registers**, and whatever he had into the car and set off *„like a slalom between tanks”* toward Zagreb. On the way from Sisak toward the villages, he heard the start of the cannonade. It was around five o'clock in the morning, when Croatian artillery began preparations for the **liberation of Banovina**.
